The FBI has linked North Korea to the theft of a record $6.3bn in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance. Malicious actors from North Korea were observed laundering the ⁠stolen assets ⁠by converting them primarily into the cryptocurrency Ethereum, ⁠the FBI said in a statement on Saturday. The US agency blamed the operation specifically on a group called TraderTraitor, the same group blamed for a $1.5bn theft from the Bybit platform in February last year. According to the statement, the assets are expected to be “further laundered” in stages. The FBI called on virtual asset service providers to block transactions being used in the latest laundering operation, providing the suspected digital addresses to watch for. In a separate statement on Saturday, Binance said it has replaced 90 percent of the amount stolen by using company money to buy new tokens. The remaining 10 percent consists of less liquid tokens, meaning they ⁠may take longer to buy, it added. “We will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets… until the covered amount reaches 100 [percent] for all tokens. The FBI blamed North Korea for the Binance crypto hack after $US6.3 billion in bitcoin and other digital currency was stolen from the world’s largest crypto exchange. The FBI said the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor carried out the "malicious cyber activity" and it found TraderTraitor was converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum. Binance said it had enough funds set aside to cover 90 per cent of the stolen assets, and it said the remaining 10 per cent consisted of tokens that were less liquid. The FBI asked crypto exchanges and blockchain analytics companies to block transactions linked to various addresses to make sure the money is not laundered to cover up its origins. A separate Binance update said withdrawals were on track to resume Sunday after the exchange suspended user withdrawals after the hack. The FBI said it expected TraderTraitor would attempt to convert the assets using de-centralised finance (DeFi) and "instant swap services" and that it was "expected these assets will then be further laundered." A crypto expert and chief policy officer at TRM Labs, Ari Redbord, said he expected the hackers would break the stolen assets into pieces and try to launder them through smaller exchanges to evade detection. The FBI blamed North Korea for the Binance crypto hack after $US6.3 billion in bitcoin and other digital currency was stolen from the world’s largest crypto exchange. The FBI said the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor carried out the "malicious cyber activity" and it found TraderTraitor was converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum. Binance said it had enough funds set aside to cover 90 per cent of the stolen assets, and it said the remaining 10 per cent consisted of tokens that were less liquid.

The FBI asked crypto exchanges and blockchain analytics companies to block transactions linked to various addresses to make sure the money is not laundered to cover up its origins. A separate Binance update said withdrawals were on track to resume Sunday after the exchange suspended user withdrawals after the hack.

The FBI said it expected TraderTraitor would attempt to convert the assets using de-centralised finance (DeFi) and "instant swap services" and that it was "expected these assets will then be further laundered." A crypto expert and chief policy officer at TRM Labs, Ari Redbord, said he expected the hackers would break the stolen assets into pieces and try to launder them through smaller exchanges to evade detection. President Donald Trump told reporters, "We don’t know if it’s North Korea," while he said investigators were learning about the case.
Trump suggested investigators were not yet certain about North Korea

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the breach was a "complex attack" involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it hard to trace and investigate. Binance said it would continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets until the covered amount reached 100 percent for all tokens, and it said it would absorb the financial impact, not users.

The FBI urged virtual asset service providers to block transactions being used in the latest laundering operation by providing suspected digital addresses to watch for. Binance said it would replace 90 percent of the amount stolen by using company money to buy new tokens, and it said the remaining 10 percent consisted of less liquid tokens that may take longer to buy. Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses, and it said its next goal was resuming withdrawal services for users on Sunday 1 November.

Binance said it had published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot so users could independently verify that their assets were backed at a minimum 1:1 ratio. The FBI said it expects TraderTraitor to attempt further conversion and laundering in stages, as the investigation continued and Binance worked to restore access to customer funds.

Hackers pilfered US$6.3 billion from the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange in a stunning attack that halted withdrawals on the platform and set off a race among digital currency companies to freeze billions in stolen funds.
The main thrust of the attack on Binance took about 20 minutes, according to third-party cyber security firms who examined public flows of cryptocurrency in and out of the exchange.

It remains unclear how the hackers managed to breach the systems of Binance to steal the US$6.3b ($11.1b). At least two firms have attributed the hack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacker group that has been behind other major crypto thefts, based in part on analysis of the flow of funds. Binance has not said who it thinks is responsible.

Binance said on Thursday (local time) that its initial investigation pointed to the compromise of one engineer’s laptop as the source of the hack. The company has since said it thinks there were additional breaches in the attack.

“This was a complex attack,” Richard Teng, the exchange’s CEO, said in a video on social media. “The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate.”

The heist was breathtaking not only for its scope but for its speed, with billions of funds vanishing in only minutes. Cryptocurrency, which runs on a decentralised exchange called blockchain, is supposed to be able to move quickly by design.
“This is not just the biggest hack in crypto. It’s actually the biggest hack in the world, ever,” Ido Ben-Natan, the chief executive of crypto security company Blockaid, said.

According to cyber security firm CrowdStrike, a US$1.5b theft in 2025 from the exchange Bybit – also a cryptocurrency hack eventually attributed to North Korean attackers – was previously the largest single financial theft ever reported.

Some details of the attack, including how the hackers got inside Binance, are still unclear. But because cryptocurrency runs on a decentralised network, all transactions are public. In the hours after the heist, a number of crypto research firms scrambled to trace the apparent flow of funds out of Binance into other cryptocurrency accounts, known in the industry as wallets. At least three companies have released reports detailing their analysis of what happened.

The US$6.3b theft from Binance kicked off an apparent cat-and-mouse game where the hackers rushed to split the stolen money up among various wallets, according to third-party analysts, knowing that cryptocurrency issuers would attempt to freeze the funds.

The blockchain security company Chainalysis said in a blog post that the volume of transactions suggested that the attackers relied on automated activity to “obscure the trail of funds” by quickly shuffling money in and out of various wallets.

The hackers appeared to swipe funds in a variety of cryptocurrencies, some of them centrally issued by companies, who rushed to lock down hundreds of millions in assets on Binance. Within about an hour, the companies Circle and Tether had frozen about US$971 million and $825 million in their respective stablecoins – a kind of digital dollar that is pegged to a secure asset such as the US dollar.
Binance has since said that about US$3b of the stolen funds were frozen by various partners, preventing the hackers from transferring them further.

But the traditional model of cryptocurrencies, like bitcoin, live out in the wild on completely decentralised networks where it’s not possible to pull the plug. TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence company, said it observed the hackers racing to convert their loot into these non-freezable cryptocurrencies, by seeking out loan platforms or “market-makers” that would make the switch.
In all, at least US$2.4b appears to be “beyond any issuer’s reach”, TRM Labs said.
Binance has said it will refund customers through a combination of its own funds and a US$1b bitcoin reserve designed to cover hacking incidents and other emergencies.
The exchange has paused withdrawals while it conducts security checks.

The hack comes during heightened fears of cyber attacks enabled by powerful artificial intelligence systems. While it’s not clear that the Binance hackers used artificial intelligence (AI), cryptocurrency is a fast-moving industry where “they’re basically building the plane as they’re flying it” Benjamin Cole, a professor at Fordham University, said.

“Basically across every endpoint on the internet at this point – companies of every stripe, be they crypto or not – there’s a growing sense that there is a new cyber security reality in play,” Eric Jardine, the head of research at Chainalysis, said.

The hack underscores several characteristics of cryptocurrency, envisioned by enthusiasts as a liberating substitute for the traditional financial system. Instead of banks and governments managing accounts and regulating currencies, cryptocurrency can move from user to user in a decentralised manner.

And despite efforts to move cryptocurrency into the mainstream, those characteristics have made the technology an attractive opportunity for criminals, terrorist groups and other actors who might otherwise be barred from banks.

While Binance has not said who it thinks is responsible for the hack, two cyber security firms attribute it to TraderTraitor. Chainalysis, one of the firms, said it observed money stolen from Binance co-mingling with funds from a US$388m heist of a different cryptocurrency exchange last month that was also attributed to North Korean attackers.

In all, TRM Labs estimates that North Korean hackers have stolen US$12.8b in cryptocurrency over more than 100 incidents since 2017 (the country’s estimated domestic gross product in 2025 was about US$26b). TraderTraitor has been identified as the cause for previous major crypto hacks, including the US$1.5b theft from Bybit. That heist, too, was executed in only minutes.

Binance has faced a number of legal issues. In 2023, its chief executive, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to violating criminal anti-money-laundering guidelines meant to prevent illicit transactions. The company also pleaded guilty to criminal charges after prosecutors accused it of allowing transactions from al-Qaeda, the Islamic State, Hamas and other groups. Binance said at the time it took responsibility “for this past chapter”.

Zhao, who stepped down as chief executive, was pardoned by US President Donald Trump, whose Administration said the crypto executive was unfairly targeted by the Biden Administration. The company was also fined US$4.3b.
Binance has no official headquarters and was founded in China in 2017. Binance.US, its American version, said it was not affected.
Binance said it is co-ordinating with global law enforcement and several US agencies said they were aware of the hack or investigating it.

“Secret Service investigators are working around the clock with our private-sector partners, including Circle, to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds stolen from Binance on Thursday,” Secret Service spokesman Thomas Lynch said in a statement. The Secret Service, in addition to protecting the president, also investigates cyber crimes.
But even with some funds recovered, the hack appears to be a record-setting heist.

“With a couple hundred elite hackers, they’re far exceeding the revenues of the things North Korea used to sell,” Nick Carlsen, an investigator at TRM Labs, said of TraderTraitor. “This is just basically the North Korean Government’s primary source of hard currency revenue now.”

Some details of the attack, including how the hackers got inside Binance, are still unclear. But because cryptocurrency runs on a decentralised network, all transactions are public. In the hours after the heist, a number of crypto research firms scrambled to trace the apparent flow of funds out of Binance into other cryptocurrency accounts, known in the industry as wallets. At least three companies have released reports detailing their analysis of what happened. The US$6.3b theft from Binance kicked off an apparent cat-and-mouse game where the hackers rushed to split the stolen money up among various wallets, according to third-party analysts, knowing that cryptocurrency issuers would attempt to freeze the funds. The blockchain security company Chainalysis said in a blog post that the volume of transactions suggested that the attackers relied on automated activity to “obscure the trail of funds” by quickly shuffling money in and out of various wallets. The hackers appeared to swipe funds in a variety of cryptocurrencies, some of them centrally issued by companies, who rushed to lock down hundreds of millions in assets on Binance. Within about an hour, the companies Circle and Tether had frozen about US$971 million and $825 million in their respective stablecoins – a kind of digital dollar that is pegged to a secure asset such as the US dollar. Binance has since said that about US$3b of the stolen funds were frozen by various partners, preventing the hackers from transferring them further. But the traditional model of cryptocurrencies, like bitcoin, live out in the wild on completely decentralised networks where it’s not possible to pull the plug. TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence company, said it observed the hackers racing to convert their loot into these non-freezable cryptocurrencies, by seeking out loan platforms or “market-makers” that would make the switch. In all, at least US$2.4b appears to be “beyond any issuer’s reach”, TRM Labs said. Binance has said it will refund customers through a combination of its own funds and a US$1b bitcoin reserve designed to cover hacking incidents and other emergencies. The exchange has paused withdrawals while it conducts security checks. The hack comes during heightened fears of cyber attacks enabled by powerful artificial intelligence systems. While it’s not clear that the Binance hackers used artificial intelligence (AI), cryptocurrency is a fast-moving industry where “they’re basically building the plane as they’re flying it” Benjamin Cole, a professor at Fordham University, said. “Basically across every endpoint on the internet at this point – companies of every stripe, be they crypto or not – there’s a growing sense that there is a new cyber security reality in play,” Eric Jardine, the head of research at Chainalysis, said. Instead of banks and governments managing accounts and regulating currencies, cryptocurrency can move from user to user in a decentralised manner. And despite efforts to move cryptocurrency into the mainstream, those characteristics have made the technology an attractive opportunity for criminals, terrorist groups and other actors who might otherwise be barred from banks. Chainalysis, one of the firms, said it observed money stolen from Binance co-mingling with funds from a US$388m heist of a different cryptocurrency exchange last month that was also attributed to North Korean attackers. Binance has faced a number of legal issues. In 2023, its chief executive, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to violating criminal anti-money-laundering guidelines meant to prevent illicit transactions. The company also pleaded guilty to criminal charges after prosecutors accused it of allowing transactions from al-Qaeda, the Islamic State, Hamas and other groups. Binance said at the time it took responsibility “for this past chapter”. Zhao, who stepped down as chief executive, was pardoned by US President Donald Trump, whose Administration said the crypto executive was unfairly targeted by the Biden Administration. The company was also fined US$4.3b. Binance has no official headquarters and was founded in China in 2017. Binance.US, its American version, said it was not affected. The Secret Service, in addition to protecting the president, also investigates cyber crimes. But even with some funds recovered, the hack appears to be a record-setting heist. “With a couple hundred elite hackers, they’re far exceeding the revenues of the things North Korea used to sell,” Nick Carlsen, an investigator at TRM Labs, said of TraderTraitor. “This is just basically the North Korean Government’s primary source of hard currency revenue now.”

passages: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to allow its customers to withdraw their funds from the platform, as it recovers from a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack.
Richard Teng, Binance’s co-chief executive, said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that users would not bear the financial impact of the hack.

Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses.
The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to allow its customers to withdraw their funds from the platform, as it recovers from a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack. The exchange was hit by the theft on Thursday, which has since been described as the biggest heist in history, with experts identifying North Korea as the likely culprit. Binance initially froze withdrawals as it investigated the breach, but on Sunday announced that it had began a phased reopening after 2pm Singapore time. The first phase will allow people who hold the ethereum, USDT and USDC tokens on the ethereum blockchain to withdraw their funds, as well as some others held on the BNB Smart Chain blockchain. The platform said it has replenished 90% of the ⁠amount stolen. The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Richard Teng, Binance’s co-chief executive, said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that users would not bear the financial impact of the hack. It came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. “The Federal Bureau of Investigation is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6bn in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29,” the law enforcement agency said in a statement. The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services. It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors” were “using to launder these stolen assets”. Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate. Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said. The money spent rebuying tokens came from using part of its $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some ⁠of its Futures Insurance Fund, and the company’s own corporate treasury, it said ​on X. The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%. The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.

extraction.body: Investing.com -- Binance said it would begin restoring customer withdrawals in stages on Sunday after a record cryptocurrency theft exceeding $6 billion forced the world's largest digital asset exchange to suspend transactions and raised concerns about security across the industry. The exchange said the first phase would run from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. Singapore time on November 1, with additional cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks restored after security and stability checks. Binance said it would prioritize assets based on customer withdrawal demand over the previous week, allowing services to resume gradually rather than reopening all transactions simultaneously. The announcement follows a breach disclosed Thursday that prompted Binance to halt withdrawals early Friday in Asia. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking group, which was previously linked to the $1.5 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit in 2025. Binance said it had replaced approximately 90% of the stolen cryptocurrencies and reiterated that customers would not bear the financial losses. The stolen assets included Bitcoin, Ether and dollar-backed stablecoins USDT and USDC. Co-CEO Richard Teng said the exchange could cover the losses through cryptocurrency holdings accumulated from its operating revenue. Fellow co-CEO Yi He indicated that Binance's annual revenue would be sufficient to absorb the financial impact. Bitcoin traded near $77,700 on Sunday, approximately 5% below its Thursday high before the attack, as major cryptocurrencies showed relatively limited price movements. The exchange holds approximately $135 billion in assets, significantly exceeding the roughly $29 billion held by rival OKX, according to DefiLlama. Binance also maintains its Secure Asset Fund for Users, established in 2018 to protect customers during exceptional incidents. The emergency reserve has typically been maintained near $1 billion. Investigators are examining a potentially compromised software engineer's laptop and other possible entry points, although Binance said it had found no evidence that private wallet keys were exposed. The incident has intensified scrutiny of cryptocurrency security amid concerns that hackers are increasingly using artificial intelligence for reconnaissance and social engineering. extraction.body: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to allow its customers to withdraw their funds from the platform, as it recovers from a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack. The exchange was hit by the theft on Thursday, which has since been described as the biggest heist in history, with experts identifying North Korea as the likely culprit. Binance initially froze withdrawals as it investigated the breach, but on Sunday announced that it had began a phased reopening after 2pm Singapore time. The first phase will allow people who hold the ethereum, USDT and USDC tokens on the ethereum blockchain to withdraw their funds, as well as some others held on the BNB Smart Chain blockchain. The platform said it has replenished 90% of the ⁠amount stolen. The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Richard Teng, Binance’s co-chief executive, said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that users would not bear the financial impact of the hack. It came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. “The Federal Bureau of Investigation is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6bn in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29,” the law enforcement agency said in a statement. The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services. It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors” were “using to launder these stolen assets”. Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate. Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said. The money spent rebuying tokens came from using part of its $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some ⁠of its Futures Insurance Fund, and the company’s own corporate treasury, it said ​on X. The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%. The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.

extraction.body: Investing.com -- Binance said it would begin restoring customer withdrawals in stages on Sunday after a record cryptocurrency theft exceeding $6 billion forced the world's largest digital asset exchange to suspend transactions and raised concerns about security across the industry. The exchange said the first phase would run from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. Singapore time on November 1, with additional cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks restored after security and stability checks. Binance said it would prioritize assets based on customer withdrawal demand over the previous week, allowing services to resume gradually rather than reopening all transactions simultaneously. The announcement follows a breach disclosed Thursday that prompted Binance to halt withdrawals early Friday in Asia. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking group, which was previously linked to the $1.5 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit in 2025. Binance said it had replaced approximately 90% of the stolen cryptocurrencies and reiterated that customers would not bear the financial losses. The stolen assets included Bitcoin, Ether and dollar-backed stablecoins USDT and USDC. Co-CEO Richard Teng said the exchange could cover the losses through cryptocurrency holdings accumulated from its operating revenue. Fellow co-CEO Yi He indicated that Binance's annual revenue would be sufficient to absorb the financial impact. Bitcoin traded near $77,700 on Sunday, approximately 5% below its Thursday high before the attack, as major cryptocurrencies showed relatively limited price movements. The exchange holds approximately $135 billion in assets, significantly exceeding the roughly $29 billion held by rival OKX, according to DefiLlama. Binance also maintains its Secure Asset Fund for Users, established in 2018 to protect customers during exceptional incidents. The emergency reserve has typically been maintained near $1 billion. Investigators are examining a potentially compromised software engineer's laptop and other possible entry points, although Binance said it had found no evidence that private wallet keys were exposed. The incident has intensified scrutiny of cryptocurrency security amid concerns that hackers are increasingly using artificial intelligence for reconnaissance and social engineering. Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the tone of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance had “changed completely,” describing it as a positive development as Tehran awaited Washington’s response. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera that “The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and understanding more broadly is a positive step,” while also saying Tehran was not yet ready for direct negotiations with American officials. Iran’s remarks came as mediators intensified efforts to avert renewed strikes, with the diplomatic push involving Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries and consultations that included talks in Tehran and then shifted to Doha.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump had not made a decision on further strikes and that the administration remained open to a diplomatic solution. Rezaei did not disclose the contents of Vance’s letter, and Araghchi said Tehran was reviewing proposals concerning its nuclear programme.

At the 22nd IISS Manama Dialogue in Bahrain, GCC Secretary General Jasem Mohamed Al Budaiwi said the GCC states “still do” call for dialogue and negotiation to resolve issues in the region. Al Budaiwi added that “But diplomacy needs partners, partners who respond in kind,” and he said the six-member bloc maintained open channels with Iran alongside partnerships with Western powers, China, Russia and other countries. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty warned that “The second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere,” and he said military action could unleash consequences beyond the control of those who initiated it.

Al Budaiwi called for navigation through the Strait of Hormuz to return to conditions before February 28, when the US-Iran war began, and he said disruptions to the strait had affected energy prices, shipping, insurance and global supply chains. Britain’s Middle East Minister Stephen Doughty said the UK had deployed air defense equipment and personnel to Saudi Arabia and that “We must strain every sinew for peace,” while promising continued diplomatic engagement.

Iran’s position remained that the shift in Washington’s tone did not remove its conditions, and Mohsen Rezaei said in a video broadcast on Iranian television that “Their tone has completely changed,” while he said he “haven’t yet responded.” Araghchi told Al Jazeera that Tehran had studied the letter in high-level meetings and warned that if Washington’s objective was to “foment discord,” it would be “one more mistake to add to the previous ones.” Araghchi also said Tehran had “no plans to meet with American officials,” and he described circulating claims about such meetings as “mere media speculation.”

In parallel, mediators continued consultations on Iran’s conditions, and Araghchi said his aides were in Qatar while mediators in Qatar and Pakistan continued their consultations on those conditions. The diplomatic opening left unresolved disagreements over nuclear and sanctions issues, with Washington seeking nuclear concessions from Tehran while Iran sought relief from the US naval blockade, access to frozen funds and permission to resume oil sales.

Iranian foreign minister Araghchi calls Vance letter a positive step toward dialogue. Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the tone of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance had “changed completely,” describing it as a positive development as Tehran awaited Washington’s response. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera that “The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and understanding more broadly is a positive step,” while also saying Tehran was not yet ready for direct negotiations with American officials. Iran’s remarks came as mediators intensified efforts to avert renewed strikes, with the diplomatic push involving Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries and consultations that included talks in Tehran and then shifted to Doha. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump had not made a decision on further strikes and that the administration remained open to a diplomatic solution. Rezaei did not disclose the contents of Vance’s letter, and Araghchi said Tehran was reviewing proposals concerning its nuclear programme. At the 22nd IISS Manama Dialogue in Bahrain, GCC Secretary General Jasem Mohamed Al Budaiwi said the GCC states “still do” call for dialogue and negotiation to resolve issues in the region. Al Budaiwi added that “But diplomacy needs partners, partners who respond in kind,” and he said the six-member bloc maintained open channels with Iran alongside partnerships with Western powers, China, Russia and other countries. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty warned that “The second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere,” and he said military action could unleash consequences beyond the control of those who initiated it. Al Budaiwi called for navigation through the Strait of Hormuz to return to conditions before February 28, when the US-Iran war began, and he said disruptions to the strait had affected energy prices, shipping, insurance and global supply chains. Britain’s Middle East Minister Stephen Doughty said the UK had deployed air defense equipment and personnel to Saudi Arabia and that “We must strain every sinew for peace,” while promising continued diplomatic engagement. Iran’s position remained that the shift in Washington’s tone did not remove its conditions, and Mohsen Rezaei said in a video broadcast on Iranian television that “Their tone has completely changed,” while he said he “haven’t yet responded.” Araghchi told Al Jazeera that Tehran had studied the letter in high-level meetings and warned that if Washington’s objective was to “foment discord,” it would be “one more mistake to add to the previous ones.” Araghchi also said Tehran had “no plans to meet with American officials,” and he described circulating claims about such meetings as “mere media speculation.” In parallel, mediators continued consultations on Iran’s conditions, and Araghchi said his aides were in Qatar while mediators in Qatar and Pakistan continued their consultations on those conditions. The diplomatic opening left unresolved disagreements over nuclear and sanctions issues, with Washington seeking nuclear concessions from Tehran while Iran sought relief from the US naval blockade, access to frozen funds and permission to resume oil sales. Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the tone of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance had “changed completely,” describing it as a positive development as Tehran awaited Washington’s response. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera that “The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and understanding more broadly is a positive step,” while also saying Tehran was not yet ready for direct negotiations with American officials. Iran’s remarks came as mediators intensified efforts to avert renewed strikes, with the diplomatic push involving Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries and consultations that included talks in Tehran and then shifted to Doha.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump had not made a decision on further strikes and that the administration remained open to a diplomatic solution. Rezaei did not disclose the contents of Vance’s letter, and Araghchi said Tehran was reviewing proposals concerning its nuclear programme.

At the 22nd IISS Manama Dialogue in Bahrain, GCC Secretary General Jasem Mohamed Al Budaiwi said the GCC states “still do” call for dialogue and negotiation to resolve issues in the region. Al Budaiwi added that “But diplomacy needs partners, partners who respond in kind,” and he said the six-member bloc maintained open channels with Iran alongside partnerships with Western powers, China, Russia and other countries. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty warned that “The second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere,” and he said military action could unleash consequences beyond the control of those who initiated it.

Al Budaiwi called for navigation through the Strait of Hormuz to return to conditions before February 28, when the US-Iran war began, and he said disruptions to the strait had affected energy prices, shipping, insurance and global supply chains. Britain’s Middle East Minister Stephen Doughty said the UK had deployed air defense equipment and personnel to Saudi Arabia and that “We must strain every sinew for peace,” while promising continued diplomatic engagement.

Iran’s position remained that the shift in Washington’s tone did not remove its conditions, and Mohsen Rezaei said in a video broadcast on Iranian television that “Their tone has completely changed,” while he said he “haven’t yet responded.” Araghchi told Al Jazeera that Tehran had studied the letter in high-level meetings and warned that if Washington’s objective was to “foment discord,” it would be “one more mistake to add to the previous ones.” Araghchi also said Tehran had “no plans to meet with American officials,” and he described circulating claims about such meetings as “mere media speculation.”

In parallel, mediators continued consultations on Iran’s conditions, and Araghchi said his aides were in Qatar while mediators in Qatar and Pakistan continued their consultations on those conditions. The diplomatic opening left unresolved disagreements over nuclear and sanctions issues, with Washington seeking nuclear concessions from Tehran while Iran sought relief from the US naval blockade, access to frozen funds and permission to resume oil sales.

extraction.body: The startup maps how identities, assets and vulnerabilities connect, and uses AI agents to find and fix risky combinations of issues. Northstar Security, a startup developing AI agents for security teams, has emerged from stealth mode with $7 million in seed funding. Wing Venture Capital led the round. MVP, Outliers, and cybersecurity veterans Gerhard Eschelbeck, Renaud Deraison, and Justin Somaini also invested. The company ingests data from existing security and IT tools to build what it calls a Security Context Graph. Updated in real time, the graph shows how identities, assets, applications, vulnerabilities, and business systems connect to one another. Northstar aims to catch so-called toxic combinations. Issues such as a vulnerability, an unmanaged device, or an account with excessive privileges may seem under control on their own, but together they can expose critical business systems. For instance, the platform could flag a laptop lacking endpoint protection whose owner is a privileged user able to reach a critical payroll system. Analysts can investigate findings like this by asking questions in plain language. Northstar’s agents can then kick off fixes, such as installing endpoint protection, notifying the user, or limiting their access, and people can supervise those actions where appropriate. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading. Customers can also give external AI agents access to the graph through Model Context Protocol (MCP) and build their own security workflows. Northstar says it connects to more than 70 enterprise security and IT products, among them Okta, GitHub, Workday, Microsoft Defender and Entra, AWS, and Google Cloud. “Security teams are drowning in data but starving for context,” said Amer Deeba, Northstar’s CEO and co-founder. Deeba co-founded Normalyze, which Proofpoint later acquired , and was previously a senior executive at Qualys. His co-founder, CTO Ed Rowe, held the same role at Farmers Business Network and led engineering as an SVP at AppDynamics. The startup will use the money to develop its platform, hire staff, and expand its go-to-market push. extraction.body: The startup maps how identities, assets and vulnerabilities connect, and uses AI agents to find and fix risky combinations of issues. Northstar Security, a startup developing AI agents for security teams, has emerged from stealth mode with $7 million in seed funding. Wing Venture Capital led the round. MVP, Outliers, and cybersecurity veterans Gerhard Eschelbeck, Renaud Deraison, and Justin Somaini also invested. The company ingests data from existing security and IT tools to build what it calls a Security Context Graph. Updated in real time, the graph shows how identities, assets, applications, vulnerabilities, and business systems connect to one another. Northstar aims to catch so-called toxic combinations. Issues such as a vulnerability, an unmanaged device, or an account with excessive privileges may seem under control on their own, but together they can expose critical business systems. For instance, the platform could flag a laptop lacking endpoint protection whose owner is a privileged user able to reach a critical payroll system. Analysts can investigate findings like this by asking questions in plain language. Northstar’s agents can then kick off fixes, such as installing endpoint protection, notifying the user, or limiting their access, and people can supervise those actions where appropriate. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading. Customers can also give external AI agents access to the graph through Model Context Protocol (MCP) and build their own security workflows. Northstar says it connects to more than 70 enterprise security and IT products, among them Okta, GitHub, Workday, Microsoft Defender and Entra, AWS, and Google Cloud. “Security teams are drowning in data but starving for context,” said Amer Deeba, Northstar’s CEO and co-founder. Deeba co-founded Normalyze, which Proofpoint later acquired , and was previously a senior executive at Qualys. His co-founder, CTO Ed Rowe, held the same role at Farmers Business Network and led engineering as an SVP at AppDynamics. The startup will use the money to develop its platform, hire staff, and expand its go-to-market push. extraction.body: On Thursday evening, I slipped on my neon yellow heels and a floral mini dress. It’s New York, so I can wear whatever I want to a midterm election event full of media types, techies, policy advocates, and, well, does anyone else even exist at these things? I walked into the dimly blue-lit Brooklyn warehouse and was surprised to see the room already filling up. Newsreel, the media company founded by former Forbes and Newsweek reporter Jack Brewster, hosted the event, and the lineup was heavy-hitting. Kenneth Schlenker, co-founder of the focus app Opal, sat down for a fireside chat about “the state of attention,” and Aryan Banjan, who built the campaign management software Barza, gave a midterm forecast. I, meanwhile, was moderating a panel on data centers. Brewster said the goal was for people to “put their phones away and talk to each other about the election, five days out.” As the evening progressed, however, one topic consumed nearly every conversation: AI, data centers, and the backlash against the growing technocracy. Lately, as a tech reporter, I’ve noticed a growing chasm between tech and everyone else. I spend most of my days talking to people who see the benefits of AI, who are so ambitious in building it and so optimistic that it will succeed that, when I talk to people beyond the tech world, I forget how ugly it all seems to them. Outside the tech bubble, data centers and AI have become such an intense ballot-box issue that they could sway some midterm races on November 3. A recent report from Data Center Watch found that almost $200 billion in data center projects were delayed, stalled, or blocked in the first half of 2026 due to political and community opposition. Meanwhile, states like Pennsylvania, Georgia, Texas, New York, and Virginia are considering more guardrails and transparency around data centers’ rapid development. Hundreds of new data centers are planned in Virginia alone, a state already nicknamed the “data center capital of the world.” A fireside chat with New York City Council member Chi Ossé, just before my panel, set the tone. AI came up near the end; Ossé said he doesn’t really use it. To me, though, he didn’t seem to be for or against it. He mostly emphasized that he would like to see tech executives held more accountable and trillionaires like Elon Musk taxed more. He described himself as a democratic socialist, but a “law and order” one. When CEOs talk about a technology that could deplete 10% of human civilization, he said, “they should be called to testify in front of Congress.” My panel was up next. I moderated a discussion with Maia Woluchem, a technology and human rights researcher, and Hilary Flint, an environmental and public health advocate, about data centers. As I took the stage, I decided to get a better read on the crowd. I asked, “Who here is pro-AI data center?” and was promptly booed. Our conversation covered a range of topics and emotions. People are upset that big tech companies appear to be cutting secret deals with local officials to build billion-dollar data centers. In some cases, zoning rules make it unclear what is being built until it’s too late to protest. At the same time, people are struggling with the cost of living and doing everything they can to hold onto what’s left of the American Dream, while tech leaders talk about AI replacing workers, or even humanity itself. Residents feel they have lost control over what happens in their communities, and they worry about the environmental and health risks. The panel agreed that data centers are the physical embodiment of people’s fears and anger toward the tech class and the rapid pace of technology. “What is a life worth?” Flint said when I brought up the benefits that some communities have seen from data center build-outs. People still protest, she said, because they “value their lives a little bit more than a temporary check.” The panel after mine featured NewsNation host Batya Ungar-Sargon; political strategist Morris Katz, who worked on Zohran Mamdani’s campaign; and Vox’s Astead Herndon. They were supposed to be talking about the future of the Democratic Party. But once again, the conversation shifted to data centers. Ungar-Sargon noted that some labor unions support data centers because of the jobs they promise. (Reports show that data centers create many jobs initially, but those jobs are not permanent once construction ends.) “There used to be a lot of pride in a community in the Rust Belt about very ugly, enormous buildings in their communities because everybody worked there,” she said, nodding to an earlier comment I’d made about data centers being ugly. “And they knew that building represented prosperity for themselves, stability for their children, and a future and a piece of the American dream.” Herndon noted that Vivek Ramaswamy was booed for making a similar point in Ohio, a Rust Belt state. “I just want to reinforce the lack of consent happening,” he said. “Because that’s true among Republicans in those places and I’ve watched it.” Katz was also skeptical. “It’s the same people who have taken so many union jobs away,” he said. “The same institutional powers that have robbed labor and working people of jobs and profit. Now coming back to essentially finish the job and take whatever scraps remain.” Along the warehouse walls, I noticed sticky notes answering posted questions, including “Will we ever be able to get Big Money out of politics?” “God, I hope so,” one note said. People rushed the bar when the panel ended, and techno music began to blast. They broke into small groups, where AI and data centers were once again the topic, this time in more private conversations. I asked Brewster if he was surprised by how much of the conversation focused on AI and data centers. “It came up in every conversation on stage, and it was the second most common topic in the questions people sent us when they RSVP’d,” he said, adding that it was happening even in New York, where data centers aren’t very visible. “AI has become an election issue for regular voters,” he said. “In rural communities, the backlash is about feeling replaced. In a place like Brooklyn, it’s more about who gets rich from it.” Before leaving, I made the rounds, asking people to name the craziest thing they’d seen in tech this year. Two tech founders mentioned the AI assistant startup Instinct, while a non-tech person named Sam Altman Another non-tech person brought up the rise of deepfakes and AI art. AI art, she said, is starting to signal cheapness. That may be why luxury brands are going the other way: Prada’s holiday campaign features hand-drawn illustrations , and Hermès has been spotlighting artists’ handmade work on Instagram. On my way out, I spoke to a software engineer who said the craziest thing she’d seen this year was a person who painted their nails orange for Halloween and was asked if it was a tribute to the Anthropic IPO. I admitted that I, too, had once worn a burnt orange dress and briefly thought of myself as the Claude logo. She later told me data centers are popping up in her Southern California hometown, too. Hearing that, I thought for the first time about how I’d feel if one popped up in mine. She grew up in a Chinese immigrant community, where neighbors are putting signs in their yards showing dragons choking a data center. The signs have since been translated into other languages, she said.

In some cases, zoning rules make it unclear what is being built until it’s too late to protest. Ungar-Sargon noted that some labor unions support data centers because of the jobs they promise. AI art, she said, is starting to signal cheapness. That may be why luxury brands are going the other way: Prada’s holiday campaign features hand-drawn illustrations , and Hermès has been spotlighting artists’ handmade work on Instagram. On my way out, I spoke to a software engineer who said the craziest thing she’d seen this year was a person who painted their nails orange for Halloween and was asked if it was a tribute to the Anthropic IPO. I admitted that I, too, had once worn a burnt orange dress and briefly thought of myself as the Claude logo. She later told me data centers are popping up in her Southern California hometown, too. Hearing that, I thought for the first time about how I’d feel if one popped up in mine. She grew up in a Chinese immigrant community, where neighbors are putting signs in their yards showing dragons choking a data center. The signs have since been translated into other languages, she said.

Binance is covering the stolen funds directly, and the remaining 10 percent consists of “less liquid” tokens, which the company says may take longer to acquire. extraction.body: While the new touch-enabled MacBook Pro with the PROLED XDR screen is available for preorder across a few major retailers, Best Buy is sweetening the deal by including a $100 gift card. The gift card will be automatically added to your cart when you preorder one of Apple’s highest-end laptops available in 14- or 16-inch configurations, and even one of its 14-inch MacBook Pro laptops with the M6 chip. Di Benedetto got a chance to check out the new laptop at Apple’s event, and came away impressed by the Tandem OLED panel’s brightness and contrast, but described the update as “kind of boring” given the relatively small changes to the system otherwise. There are some unique changes to macOS that help make the new touch experience smoother, like magnifying the traffic light-colored buttons on windows when you move your finger near them. The PROLED laptops are also a bit thinner and lighter than standard models, and the Apple logo on the back glows like on older versions. Read our MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display hands-on.

extraction.body: Vic Mensa is one of those people who has done so many things that it’s hard to remember where you were first introduced to him. Or maybe his house-influenced single “Down On My Luck”? Maybe you didn’t even realize that Mensa was a rapper. Or perhaps you’re mostly aware of him through his activism, social media presence (peeling oranges and waxing poetic), or his podcast The Vic Mensa Show. Part of the secret to being so prolific, it turns out, is Voice Memos. Songs, essay ideas, orange tree thoughts, voice notes to myself at some wild hour, little things my son says that I do not want to lose. My phone is a million distractions in one rectangle, but Voice Memos is one of the few parts of it that still feels honest. That’s definitely where my voice has really found its legs. I started out peeling an orange and talking through whatever was on my mind, and it turned into this whole conversation with people about politics, history, music, grief, jokes, fatherhood, all of it. That response helped show me there was room for The Vic Mensa Show too. What is the last GIF or meme you used? [Image: Ummm… that is not Vic Mensa.

sources.title: Arsenal v Aston Villa Women Preview - Arseblog News
passages: THE LOWDOWN Arsenal welcome Aston Villa to Emirates Stadium on Sunday at 12noon in the WSL.
LAST TIME OUT When the teams last met in May at Villa Park, Arsenal ran out 3-0 winners with a brace from Russo and a goal from Frida Maanum.
In this fixture at the Emirates last season, Frida Maanum’s early goal was cancelled out by a stoppage time equaliser from Paula Tomas.
‘Very often it happens that teams do something different against us.
We have to focus on ourselves and keep building on our last performance.
The Gunners will want to continue to ride the wave they have just about clambered onto and water the green shoots of confidence and vivacity we saw on Wednesday.
A WORD FROM THE BOSS ‘Knowing from his (Villa manager Brian Sorensen) Everton team, I think it was always hard to play against Natalia [Arroyo]’s Aston Villa team as well.
Arsenal lose Dowman appeal as three-match ban upheld
While the victory at Spurs was won with gritted teeth and matted hair, Wednesday night’s performance against Benfica was far more fluent and finessed.
Arsenal simply have to go on a good run now having surrendered so many points already this season and they have to take the energy and enthusiasm of the last two games into this encounter.
Alessia Russo bagged the winner at Spurs and helped herself to a Champions League hat-trick on Wednesday, she is fast becoming Arsenal’s ‘franchise player’ if she isn’t already.
It will be interesting to see how far Slegers sticks with some of these burgeoning stabilisers on Sunday.

Arsenal also needed leadership to guide them out of their rough patch and Foord’s unwavering commitment and willingness to compete for duels has given Arsenal an injection of intensity at a time when confidence was sagging.
Sometimes you have to punch your way out of a rut and few players swing like Caitlin.

Renee Slegers’ side earned back-to-back victories for the first time this season with a 2-1 win over Spurs in the North London derby followed by a consummate 3-0 victory over Benfica in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

While the victory at Spurs was won with gritted teeth and matted hair, Wednesday night’s performance against Benfica was far more fluent and finessed. Arsenal simply have to go on a good run now having surrendered so many points already this season and they have to take the energy and enthusiasm of the last two games into this encounter.

Last season, Villa came to the Emirates and forced one of Arsenal’s six damaging league draws with a late equaliser after an insipid display. The Gunners will want to continue to ride the wave they have just about clambered onto and water the green shoots of confidence and vivacity we saw on Wednesday.

Alessia Russo bagged the winner at Spurs and helped herself to a Champions League hat-trick on Wednesday, she is fast becoming Arsenal’s ‘franchise player’ if she isn’t already. A front two of Smith and Russo has shown some positive signs in the last two games, with Hinds and Foord stablising the left side of the team. It will be interesting to see how far Slegers sticks with some of these burgeoning stabilisers on Sunday.

‘We remember the game last year, how it was difficult at Emirates for us at home. The away game was good, it was dominant. We have to be prepared, we have to be humble. What they’re going to do, it’s always a guessing game. Of course, they’re in a transition now and they’ve changed their system. Let’s see what they do against us.

‘Very often it happens that teams do something different against us. Let’s see what their game plan is. We have to focus on ourselves and keep building on our last performance. It’s good, it’s two good wins. It was Arsenal, this was us last night, and now we have to back it up with the next game coming up against Villa.’

Caitlin’s qualities have also provided a nice blend with Smith as a centre-forward and Russo in behind.

Arsenal also needed leadership to guide them out of their rough patch and Foord’s unwavering commitment and willingness to compete for duels has given Arsenal an injection of intensity at a time when confidence was sagging. Sometimes you have to punch your way out of a rut and few players swing like Caitlin.

Slegers was full of praise for Foord in her pre-match press conference too , ‘The way she plays is contagious and she’s been so important for us in that game and with that performance and everything she brought and everything we expected, we needed against Benfica, because we expected a fight there as well. We wanted her to be on a pitch again and she had a great 90 minutes again for us.’

If Villa play a low block it will be very interesting to see how we get on against it given our upturn in results. I guess it could go one of two ways. We struggle, confidence drains and we have a set back. Or we do well and it’s a further boost to confidence. Let’s hope it’s the latter.

While the victory at Spurs was won with gritted teeth and matted hair, Wednesday night’s performance against Benfica was far more fluent and finessed. Arsenal simply have to go on a good run now having surrendered so many points already this season and they have to take the energy and enthusiasm of the last two games into this encounter.

Last season, Villa came to the Emirates and forced one of Arsenal’s six damaging league draws with a late equaliser after an insipid display. The Gunners will want to continue to ride the wave they have just about clambered onto and water the green shoots of confidence and vivacity we saw on Wednesday.

Alessia Russo bagged the winner at Spurs and helped herself to a Champions League hat-trick on Wednesday, she is fast becoming Arsenal’s ‘franchise player’ if she isn’t already. A front two of Smith and Russo has shown some positive signs in the last two games, with Hinds and Foord stablising the left side of the team. It will be interesting to see how far Slegers sticks with some of these burgeoning stabilisers on Sunday.

extraction.body: The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon takes place on Sunday, November 1, bringing nearly 60,000 runners from around the world to the streets of New York for one of the most iconic races on the international running calendar. The professional women’s race is scheduled to start at 8:35 a.m. Follow this live results guide for real-time updates on the men’s and women’s winners, finishing times, podium finishers and official standings. The winners of the 2026 New York City Marathon have not yet been confirmed. The men’s and women’s results tables below will be updated in real time as the competition unfolds, with the official champions, finishing times and final standings added once they are verified. The results will be updated throughout race day as athletes cross the finish line. Final positions and finishing times will be checked against the official New York Road Runners results. Follow the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon as the elite runners compete across Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan. For live runner tracking, visit NYRR Live Results. For verified finishing times and final standings, check the official NYRR results portal. He will try to become the first men’s runner since John Kagwe in 1998 to win consecutive New York City Marathon titles. European interest centers on the Netherlands’ Abdi Nageeye (2:04:20) and Sweden’s Andreas Almgren, who is making his marathon debut after establishing himself on the track and in the half marathon. Kenya’s Hellen Obiri is the leading name in the women’s competition. She returns after winning in 2023 and 2025, when she set the course record of 2:19:51. Her main challengers include compatriots Sheila Chepkirui, the 2024 champion with a personal best of 2:17:19, and Viola Cheptoo (2:19:05). Ethiopia’s Gotytom Gebreslase (2:18:11) and American runner Jessica McClain (2:22:43) are also among the names to watch. These are pre-race contenders, not confirmed 2026 winners. The final positions and times will be published only after they are verified. The race takes place on Sunday, November 1, with professional and mass-participation divisions starting at different times. The 2026 race falls on the same day that daylight saving time ends in the United States. Clocks move back one hour at 2:00 a.m., so New York will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST) when the marathon begins. The New York Road Runners (NYRR), the race organizer, provides the official results and runner-tracking services. The men’s and women’s champions, finishing times and final podium positions will be added to this article as the official information becomes available.

Plus Icon Today's Digital Daily The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon promises to bring together nearly 60,000 runners from all over the world. Here's how to livestream the event for free online. If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, WWD may receive an affiliate commission. It goes without saying that the annual New York City Marathon is one of the most special days of the year: uniting strangers, both spectators and runners alike, in the pursuit of 26.2 miles. Traditionally taking place on the first Sunday of November, this year’s TCS New York City Marathon lands on November 1, kicking off at 8:00 a.m. EST for the professional wheelchair and handcycle divisions, with the pros assembling at the starting line next — followed by five waves of amateur runners. Related Articles Shoe Industry News Jimmy Choo Momentum Grows as Shoes Reclaim the Fashion Spotlight Fashion The Art of Gifting Well: 21 Luxury Christmas Gifts for Men Who Appreciate the Finer Things Weaving its way through all five of the city’s boroughs, the marathon’s route has been adjusted for the first time in 15 years (the change affects a portion of the course in the South Bronx). 2026 also marks the 50th anniversary of said five-borough concept, as the marathon was originally based only in Central Park before expanding, and drawing in more participants, to celebrate the U.S. Bicentennial. If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. It will be broadcast on WABC-TV locally and on ESPN2 nationally; cable cutters, though, can tune in with the help of a few editor-recommended streaming platforms like DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay. – Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost. – Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed. – $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor. According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.” Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir. Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park. Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31. At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. He had the Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 shoe on, which was also spotted on winners’ feet at marathons across Tokyo, London, Berlin, and Chicago last year. New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99. Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release. Get inspired by the best of the best in running — and their sneaker choices — by watching the New York City Marathon on November 1, courtesy of DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . Stacia Datskovska is a Senior Commerce Writer at WWD. Previously, she worked at ELLE DECOR as an assistant digital editor, covering all things luxury, culture, and lifestyle through a design lens. The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon promises to bring together nearly 60,000 runners from all over the world. Here's how to livestream the event for free online.

It goes without saying that the annual New York City Marathon is one of the most special days of the year: uniting strangers, both spectators and runners alike, in the pursuit of 26.2 miles.

Traditionally taking place on the first Sunday of November, this year’s TCS New York City Marathon lands on November 1, kicking off at 8:00 a.m. EST for the professional wheelchair and handcycle divisions, with the pros assembling at the starting line next — followed by five waves of amateur runners. Related Articles Shoe Industry News Jimmy Choo Momentum Grows as Shoes Reclaim the Fashion Spotlight Fashion The Art of Gifting Well: 21 Luxury Christmas Gifts for Men Who Appreciate the Finer Things

Weaving its way through all five of the city’s boroughs, the marathon’s route has been adjusted for the first time in 15 years (the change affects a portion of the course in the South Bronx). 2026 also marks the 50th anniversary of said five-borough concept, as the marathon was originally based only in Central Park before expanding, and drawing in more participants, to celebrate the U.S. Bicentennial.

If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. It will be broadcast on WABC-TV locally and on ESPN2 nationally; cable cutters, though, can tune in with the help of a few editor-recommended streaming platforms like DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay.
– Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels

ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost.
– Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels

Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed.
– $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels

Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor.

According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.”

Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir.

Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park.

Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31.

At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. He had the Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 shoe on, which was also spotted on winners’ feet at marathons across Tokyo, London, Berlin, and Chicago last year.

New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99.

Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release.
Get inspired by the best of the best in running — and their sneaker choices — by watching the New York City Marathon on November 1, courtesy of DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV .

extraction.body: On Sunday, November 1, nearly 60,000 runners taking on the New York City Marathon will get the rare privilege of having city traffic stop for them as they cover 26.2 miles through the five boroughs. And with coverage stretching from early morning into Sunday night, you don't necessarily have to be standing along First Avenue or waiting near Central Park to catch everyone in action.Here's what you need to know about watching the race, including start times, broadcasts, and how to follow individual runners.What Time Does the 2026 NYC Marathon Start?Things get going at 8 a.m. Handcycles and select athletes with disabilities start at 8:22 a.m., before the professional women take off at 8:35 a.m. and the men follow at 9:05 a.m.The rest of the field will leave Staten Island in five waves, beginning at 9:10 a.m. and continuing through 11:30 a.m.How to Watch the 2026 NYC MarathonThe main national broadcast starts at 8 a.m. ET on ESPN2, with coverage running until 11:30 a.m. If you'd rather stream, the ESPN app has the same coverage with an ESPN Unlimited plan, plus an extra hour of prerace programming beginning at 7 a.m. and more action through 1 p.m. There's a Spanish-language feed during the main 8 to 11:30 a.m. window as well.In New York and the surrounding tri-state area, ABC7/WABC-TV is another option. Coverage begins at 7 a.m., ahead of the race broadcast from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., which you can also stream on the ABC 7 New York app.For anyone more interested in the finish line than the rest of the course, ABC7NY.com and the ABC 7 New York app have you covered from 10:30 a.m. until 6 p.m. with a dedicated live stream. That should give you plenty of time to catch the professionals and stick around for the thousands of other runners making their way into Central Park.ABC also has a national Live from the TCS New York City Marathon special scheduled for 3 to 5 p.m. Before hopping on the subway, you'll probably want to check how far along they are, which is where the official New York Road Runners app comes in handy.You can track individual runners throughout the race, check their progress at timing points, and pull up leaderboards and results. The app is available for iOS and Android, and it also has live feeds for each of the four professional races if you want to keep an eye on the elites while you're out cheering.Who to Watch at the 2026 NYC MarathonLast year's champions, Benson Kipruto and Hellen Obiri, are both coming back, and each has a memorable performance to defend. Kipruto won the closest men's finish in NYC Marathon history in 2025, while Obiri ran 2:19:51 to break the women's course record that had stood for 22 years.Conner Mantz and Zouhair Talbi are among the Americans to watch in the men's race. On the women's side, Weini Kelati is making her marathon debut against a field that includes fellow American Jess McClain and 2024 NYC winner Sheila Chepkirui. Seven-time NYC wheelchair champion Marcel Hug is also returning for another shot at the podium.Sweden's Andreas Almgren is another interesting addition, particularly because nobody has seen him race a marathon yet. The world half marathon champion has been running more than 135 miles a week to prepare for New York and told Runner's World that he's feeling confident about the work he's put in. Still, he isn't pretending the jump to 26.2 miles comes with any guarantees."The marathon is a different beast," Almgren said. "You don't really know until you're reaching that 35K mark if you're going to make it or not."And the celebrity lineup covers quite a bit of ground outside professional running. Academy Award winner Jennifer Connelly is returning to the course, along with Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski, Tony-winning Broadway star Patina Miller, and former New York Giants running back Tiki Barber.
