extraction.body: The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon takes place on Sunday, November 1, bringing nearly 60,000 runners from around the world to the streets of New York for one of the most iconic races on the international running calendar. The professional women’s race is scheduled to start at 8:35 a.m. Follow this live results guide for real-time updates on the men’s and women’s winners, finishing times, podium finishers and official standings. The winners of the 2026 New York City Marathon have not yet been confirmed. The men’s and women’s results tables below will be updated in real time as the competition unfolds, with the official champions, finishing times and final standings added once they are verified. The results will be updated throughout race day as athletes cross the finish line. Final positions and finishing times will be checked against the official New York Road Runners results. Follow the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon as the elite runners compete across Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan. For live runner tracking, visit NYRR Live Results. For verified finishing times and final standings, check the official NYRR results portal. He will try to become the first men’s runner since John Kagwe in 1998 to win consecutive New York City Marathon titles. European interest centers on the Netherlands’ Abdi Nageeye (2:04:20) and Sweden’s Andreas Almgren, who is making his marathon debut after establishing himself on the track and in the half marathon. Kenya’s Hellen Obiri is the leading name in the women’s competition. She returns after winning in 2023 and 2025, when she set the course record of 2:19:51. Her main challengers include compatriots Sheila Chepkirui, the 2024 champion with a personal best of 2:17:19, and Viola Cheptoo (2:19:05). Ethiopia’s Gotytom Gebreslase (2:18:11) and American runner Jessica McClain (2:22:43) are also among the names to watch. These are pre-race contenders, not confirmed 2026 winners. The final positions and times will be published only after they are verified. The race takes place on Sunday, November 1, with professional and mass-participation divisions starting at different times. The 2026 race falls on the same day that daylight saving time ends in the United States. Clocks move back one hour at 2:00 a.m., so New York will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST) when the marathon begins. The New York Road Runners (NYRR), the race organizer, provides the official results and runner-tracking services. The men’s and women’s champions, finishing times and final podium positions will be added to this article as the official information becomes available.

Plus Icon Today's Digital Daily The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon promises to bring together nearly 60,000 runners from all over the world. Here's how to livestream the event for free online. If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, WWD may receive an affiliate commission. It goes without saying that the annual New York City Marathon is one of the most special days of the year: uniting strangers, both spectators and runners alike, in the pursuit of 26.2 miles. Traditionally taking place on the first Sunday of November, this year’s TCS New York City Marathon lands on November 1, kicking off at 8:00 a.m. EST for the professional wheelchair and handcycle divisions, with the pros assembling at the starting line next — followed by five waves of amateur runners. Related Articles Shoe Industry News Jimmy Choo Momentum Grows as Shoes Reclaim the Fashion Spotlight Fashion The Art of Gifting Well: 21 Luxury Christmas Gifts for Men Who Appreciate the Finer Things Weaving its way through all five of the city’s boroughs, the marathon’s route has been adjusted for the first time in 15 years (the change affects a portion of the course in the South Bronx). 2026 also marks the 50th anniversary of said five-borough concept, as the marathon was originally based only in Central Park before expanding, and drawing in more participants, to celebrate the U.S. Bicentennial. If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. It will be broadcast on WABC-TV locally and on ESPN2 nationally; cable cutters, though, can tune in with the help of a few editor-recommended streaming platforms like DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay. – Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost. – Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed. – $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor. According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.” Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir. Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park. Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31. At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. He had the Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 shoe on, which was also spotted on winners’ feet at marathons across Tokyo, London, Berlin, and Chicago last year. New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99. Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release. Get inspired by the best of the best in running — and their sneaker choices — by watching the New York City Marathon on November 1, courtesy of DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . Her bylines over the past five years have appeared in USA Today, Baltimore Sun, Teen Vogue, Boston Globe, Food & Wine, and more. The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon promises to bring together nearly 60,000 runners from all over the world. Here's how to livestream the event for free online.

It goes without saying that the annual New York City Marathon is one of the most special days of the year: uniting strangers, both spectators and runners alike, in the pursuit of 26.2 miles.

Traditionally taking place on the first Sunday of November, this year’s TCS New York City Marathon lands on November 1, kicking off at 8:00 a.m. EST for the professional wheelchair and handcycle divisions, with the pros assembling at the starting line next — followed by five waves of amateur runners. Related Articles Shoe Industry News Jimmy Choo Momentum Grows as Shoes Reclaim the Fashion Spotlight Fashion The Art of Gifting Well: 21 Luxury Christmas Gifts for Men Who Appreciate the Finer Things

Weaving its way through all five of the city’s boroughs, the marathon’s route has been adjusted for the first time in 15 years (the change affects a portion of the course in the South Bronx). 2026 also marks the 50th anniversary of said five-borough concept, as the marathon was originally based only in Central Park before expanding, and drawing in more participants, to celebrate the U.S. Bicentennial.

If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. It will be broadcast on WABC-TV locally and on ESPN2 nationally; cable cutters, though, can tune in with the help of a few editor-recommended streaming platforms like DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay.
– Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels

ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost.
– Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels

Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed.
– $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels

Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor.

According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.”

Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir.

Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park.

Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31.

At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. He had the Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 shoe on, which was also spotted on winners’ feet at marathons across Tokyo, London, Berlin, and Chicago last year.

New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99.

Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release.
Get inspired by the best of the best in running — and their sneaker choices — by watching the New York City Marathon on November 1, courtesy of DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV .

extraction.body: On Sunday, November 1, nearly 60,000 runners taking on the New York City Marathon will get the rare privilege of having city traffic stop for them as they cover 26.2 miles through the five boroughs. And with coverage stretching from early morning into Sunday night, you don't necessarily have to be standing along First Avenue or waiting near Central Park to catch everyone in action.Here's what you need to know about watching the race, including start times, broadcasts, and how to follow individual runners.What Time Does the 2026 NYC Marathon Start?Things get going at 8 a.m. Handcycles and select athletes with disabilities start at 8:22 a.m., before the professional women take off at 8:35 a.m. and the men follow at 9:05 a.m.The rest of the field will leave Staten Island in five waves, beginning at 9:10 a.m. and continuing through 11:30 a.m.How to Watch the 2026 NYC MarathonThe main national broadcast starts at 8 a.m. ET on ESPN2, with coverage running until 11:30 a.m. If you'd rather stream, the ESPN app has the same coverage with an ESPN Unlimited plan, plus an extra hour of prerace programming beginning at 7 a.m. and more action through 1 p.m. There's a Spanish-language feed during the main 8 to 11:30 a.m. window as well.In New York and the surrounding tri-state area, ABC7/WABC-TV is another option. Coverage begins at 7 a.m., ahead of the race broadcast from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., which you can also stream on the ABC 7 New York app.For anyone more interested in the finish line than the rest of the course, ABC7NY.com and the ABC 7 New York app have you covered from 10:30 a.m. until 6 p.m. with a dedicated live stream. That should give you plenty of time to catch the professionals and stick around for the thousands of other runners making their way into Central Park.ABC also has a national Live from the TCS New York City Marathon special scheduled for 3 to 5 p.m. Before hopping on the subway, you'll probably want to check how far along they are, which is where the official New York Road Runners app comes in handy.You can track individual runners throughout the race, check their progress at timing points, and pull up leaderboards and results. The app is available for iOS and Android, and it also has live feeds for each of the four professional races if you want to keep an eye on the elites while you're out cheering.Who to Watch at the 2026 NYC MarathonLast year's champions, Benson Kipruto and Hellen Obiri, are both coming back, and each has a memorable performance to defend. Kipruto won the closest men's finish in NYC Marathon history in 2025, while Obiri ran 2:19:51 to break the women's course record that had stood for 22 years.Conner Mantz and Zouhair Talbi are among the Americans to watch in the men's race. On the women's side, Weini Kelati is making her marathon debut against a field that includes fellow American Jess McClain and 2024 NYC winner Sheila Chepkirui. Seven-time NYC wheelchair champion Marcel Hug is also returning for another shot at the podium.Sweden's Andreas Almgren is another interesting addition, particularly because nobody has seen him race a marathon yet. The world half marathon champion has been running more than 135 miles a week to prepare for New York and told Runner's World that he's feeling confident about the work he's put in. Still, he isn't pretending the jump to 26.2 miles comes with any guarantees."The marathon is a different beast," Almgren said. "You don't really know until you're reaching that 35K mark if you're going to make it or not."And the celebrity lineup covers quite a bit of ground outside professional running. Academy Award winner Jennifer Connelly is returning to the course, along with Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski, Tony-winning Broadway star Patina Miller, and former New York Giants running back Tiki Barber.

extraction.body: Shedeur Sanders has hired an NFL agent for the first time, and while that typically sounds like something a player wanting a new contract would do, that isn't the main reason the Cleveland Browns quarterback is making this move. Sanders, in only his second season since being drafted in 2025, has hired Adie von Gontard of Young Money APAA Sports, as his first NFL representation. This is a logical choice because Gontard already represents Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter. Hunter and Sanders were teammates and friends at the University of Colorado and came out in the same 2025 draft. BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QUARTERBACK DESPITE HOME CROWD BOOING AND HIS '17 AWAY GAMES' COMMENTS But the fact that Sanders is hiring an agent now, after going through the draft process, enduring a disappointing first day in which he hoped to be selected in the first round but fell to the fifth and signing his rookie deal without representation, is curious. But multiple NFL sources are telling OutKick they believe Sanders has hired representation because he's getting ready to press for a trade from the Cleveland Browns. It should be noted the NFL is rife with rumors and none of the sources speaking about Sanders are directly tied to his family. DESHAUN WATSON REMAINS THE CLEVELAND BROWNS STARTING QUARTERBACK BUT THAT COMES WITH AN EXPIRATION DATE Only two weeks ago, Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hired an agent for the first time and over the weekend the Houston Texans confirmed they had traded for him. Minkah Fitzpatrick (2019), Za'Darius Smith (2023) and Haason Reddick (2024) all hired new agents because they were trying to get traded. Sanders currently finds himself as the backup quarterback in Cleveland after losing a competition for the starting job to veteran Deshaun Watson. Coach Todd Monken's decision to start Watson was not unexpected, but nonetheless disappointing to Sanders. Sanders has mostly stepped back into the shadows as most backup quarterbacks do. That opportunity, however, doesn’t appear to be on the horizon in Cleveland. Watson, 31, hasn't been great in leading the Browns to a 3-2 record. extraction.body: While Shedeur Sanders made a move this week that seemingly signals a trade from the Cleveland Browns could be coming, a top NFL insider has shut down the possibility before next month's NFL trade deadline. To the joy of Browns fans, the team enters their game on the Week 6 NFL schedule against rivals the Baltimore Ravens with a 3-2 record. For a fanbase used to losing, being over .500 at this point in the season and actually having hope to compete for a playoff spot is reason for celebration. Yet, one player who may not be thrilled is Sanders. The youngster lost the QB battle this summer to Deshaun Watson, despite the objections of fans. And so far, the veteran QB has played well enough that he is not in danger of being benched. It means that, barring injury, Sanders won't play in games again until next year. That may be why he decided to hire an agent for the first time in his career this week. The move immediately created speculation that the quarterback turned to a professional negotiator to set up his exit from Cleveland so he can get an opportunity elsewhere before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. However, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported on Saturday, "After talking to multiple league and team sources, I'd be surprised if he dealt quarterback Shedeur Sanders before this year's trade deadline." Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images On paper, it makes sense to trade Sanders. If he couldn't beat out Watson, coming off two Achilles surgeries, for the starting job this summer, he probably doesn't have a serious future in Cleveland. Furthermore, if they got a strong offer from a QB-needy team, then they should make that trade. However, it is hard to trust that Watson will remain healthy for the rest of the season when he has never done that during his five years with the Browns. Sooner or later he will probably miss games this season, and having a backup they can trust to hopefully keep them in the playoff hunt has value. If the Browns began to slip from the playoff picture before the deadline, maybe moving Sanders makes more sense. However, a case could also be made that it is a reason not to trade him, because he could just be promoted to the starting job to try and salvage their postseason hopes in the second half of the season.

extraction.body: While Shedeur Sanders made a move this week that seemingly signals a trade from the Cleveland Browns could be coming, a top NFL insider has shut down the possibility before next month's NFL trade deadline. To the joy of Browns fans, the team enters their game on the Week 6 NFL schedule against rivals the Baltimore Ravens with a 3-2 record. For a fanbase used to losing, being over .500 at this point in the season and actually having hope to compete for a playoff spot is reason for celebration. Yet, one player who may not be thrilled is Sanders. The youngster lost the QB battle this summer to Deshaun Watson, despite the objections of fans. And so far, the veteran QB has played well enough that he is not in danger of being benched. It means that, barring injury, Sanders won't play in games again until next year. That may be why he decided to hire an agent for the first time in his career this week. The move immediately created speculation that the quarterback turned to a professional negotiator to set up his exit from Cleveland so he can get an opportunity elsewhere before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. However, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported on Saturday, "After talking to multiple league and team sources, I'd be surprised if he dealt quarterback Shedeur Sanders before this year's trade deadline." Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images On paper, it makes sense to trade Sanders. If he couldn't beat out Watson, coming off two Achilles surgeries, for the starting job this summer, he probably doesn't have a serious future in Cleveland. Furthermore, if they got a strong offer from a QB-needy team, then they should make that trade. However, it is hard to trust that Watson will remain healthy for the rest of the season when he has never done that during his five years with the Browns. Sooner or later he will probably miss games this season, and having a backup they can trust to hopefully keep them in the playoff hunt has value. If the Browns began to slip from the playoff picture before the deadline, maybe moving Sanders makes more sense. However, a case could also be made that it is a reason not to trade him, because he could just be promoted to the starting job to try and salvage their postseason hopes in the second half of the season.

The Eagles are without Jalen Hurts due to a blood clot, and NFL analyst Zachary Rotman of FanSided shared a trade pitch that sees the Browns dealing Sanders to Philadelphia. Browns acquire: 2027 fifth-round pick Eagles acquire: Shedeur Sanders The proposed deal makes a ton of sense as Cleveland moves off Sanders and has Gabriel and Taylen Green as the backup quarterbacks. Philadelphia, meanwhile, acquires Sanders to either back up Tanner McKee or take over as the starter amid Hurts' absence. The cost is also fair, as Cleveland selected him in the fifth round, so they get the same draft pick back. Cleveland seems set with Watson as the starter, and the Browns seem unlikely to view Sanders as a long-term answer at quarterback. So, Cleveland is likely to look to draft a new starting quarterback next year, so moving off Sanders now makes sense. Analyst Explains Sanders Mock Trade The proposed deal from Rotman makes sense, and he believes Cleveland is open to moving on from Sanders, who seemingly also wants out. "Sanders likely wants out, and why shouldn't the Browns grant him his wish if they're actually comfortable with Watson? They'd still have Dillon Gabriel internally, giving them a young quarterback to turn to if Watson falters or goes down with an injury, and can net a draft pick in exchange for a player who, if we're being honest, the Browns likely don't want to see a single meaningful snap this season at all," Rotman wrote. "A fifth-round pick might seem insignificant on the surface, but the Browns used a fifth-rounder on Sanders himself in 2025. Sanders likely wants out, and the Browns don't seem interested in playing him. Getting a draft pick in exchange for a player who probably wants to be elsewhere and who the Browns don't seem eager to put onto the field in a meaningful capacity sounds like a no-brainer to me." sources.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea - BBC
passages: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist .
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, said it had "high confidence" that a North Korean is linked to the hack.
Several experts have warned customers not to regard Binance's promise to cover losses as legally binding and said they may need to pursue litigation to recover them.
In nearly all cases investigators have blamed hackers from North Korea, pointing to the infamous Lazarus Group - also know as TraderTraitor.
The names refer to clusters of cyber criminals accused of working directly for the regime.
North Korea is an impoverished country with very little industry and heavy international sanctions and experts say the regime uses cyber crime as a way to bring money in.
Who could be behind the Binance hack and what we know so far
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
A lot of the fear right now from Binance users - and the crypto industry at large - is whether or not Binance will actually be capable of covering this enormous financial loss.

America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI.

While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort.
Binance told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss".
Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said: "This was not carried out by one person.
Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach."

Daniel Tunkel, of the London-based Edwin Coe law firm, said that would "come down to what [customers] have been promised in their contracts", and "where Binance can be sued for non-performance, if it comes to it".
Binance has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.

But crypto history watchers have been pointing out online that this is exactly the kind of message that FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried gave before his crypto exchange collapsed in 2022, leading to huge losses for customers and the industry.
The company has said repeatedly that customer funds will be covered and that the firm is strong enough to weather the storm.

The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds. While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort. The hack also involved some US-linked assets, such as stablecoins Tether and Circle – cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar. Initially, the company had indicated the breach "may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" but later statements have pointed to a broader breach. passages: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.
Binance has been hit by what could be the biggest crypto hack ever - here's what we know so far

Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, said the hack was carried out by more than one person, and the hackers used sophisticated methods to hide their tracks, such as a "self-destruct mechanism".
In an update on Sunday, Binance said withdrawals had been restored on several of its networks, after they were suspended following the hack.
"Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday.

Binance's initial investigation suggested an engineer's laptop was compromised, which allowed access to unauthorised withdrawals, but a later update said they had uncovered "additional points of breach".
The US Secret Service said on Friday it is "working around the clock" with private sector partners "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds" stolen from Binance.

Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits.
Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury.
Binance, founded in China in 2017, lets users buy, sell and trade digital assets - it is estimated to have hundreds of millions of users worldwide.

The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider. Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit. The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds. America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI. While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort. The hack also involved some US-linked assets, such as stablecoins Tether and Circle – cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar. Binance told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss". It had initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals - but then said in an update that "deposits remain unaffected". Who could be behind the Binance hack and what we know so far Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said: "This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach." Teng also describes how the hackers used "a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate". Initially, the company had indicated the breach "may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" but later statements have pointed to a broader breach. In a later update, the firm said it had "set aside" more than $6.34B in company funds to cover the stolen assets and was "actively buying" a range of crypto tokens. The Binance hack spooked cryptocurrency markets on Friday. The price of Bitcoin was down 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York. Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase was down 12% as investors also reacted to earnings results in which the firm reported revenue slightly below expectations. Robinhood, a financial services company that trades in cryptocurrency, was down 7.8%. The company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets under its custody. Binance has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. The hack also involved some US-linked assets, such as stablecoins Tether and Circle – cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar.
Binance told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss".
It had initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals - but then said in an update that "deposits remain unaffected".
Who could be behind the Binance hack and what we know so far

Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said: "This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach."
Teng also describes how the hackers used "a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate".
Initially, the company had indicated the breach "may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" but later statements have pointed to a broader breach.
In a later update, the firm said it had "set aside" more than $6.34B in company funds to cover the stolen assets and was "actively buying" a range of crypto tokens.
The Binance hack spooked cryptocurrency markets on Friday. The price of Bitcoin was down 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York.

Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase was down 12% as investors also reacted to earnings results in which the firm reported revenue slightly below expectations. Robinhood, a financial services company that trades in cryptocurrency, was down 7.8%.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
A lot of the fear right now from Binance users - and the crypto industry at large - is whether or not Binance will actually be capable of covering this enormous financial loss.
The company has said repeatedly that customer funds will be covered and that the firm is strong enough to weather the storm.

But crypto history watchers have been pointing out online that this is exactly the kind of message that FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried gave before his crypto exchange collapsed in 2022, leading to huge losses for customers and the industry.
Several experts have warned customers not to regard Binance's promise to cover losses as legally binding and said they may need to pursue litigation to recover them.

Daniel Tunkel, of the London-based Edwin Coe law firm, said that would "come down to what [customers] have been promised in their contracts", and "where Binance can be sued for non-performance, if it comes to it".
Binance has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
Meanwhile, AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said that several elements of the attack resembled earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
In the last five years the crypto industry has been beset by enormous losses from hackers.

In nearly all cases investigators have blamed hackers from North Korea, pointing to the infamous Lazarus Group - also know as TraderTraitor. The names refer to clusters of cyber criminals accused of working directly for the regime.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, said it had "high confidence" that a North Korean is linked to the hack.
North Korea is an impoverished country with very little industry and heavy international sanctions and experts say the regime uses cyber crime as a way to bring money in.

sources.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack - BBC
passages: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.
Binance has been hit by what could be the biggest crypto hack ever - here's what we know so far

Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, said the hack was carried out by more than one person, and the hackers used sophisticated methods to hide their tracks, such as a "self-destruct mechanism".
In an update on Sunday, Binance said withdrawals had been restored on several of its networks, after they were suspended following the hack.
"Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday.

Binance's initial investigation suggested an engineer's laptop was compromised, which allowed access to unauthorised withdrawals, but a later update said they had uncovered "additional points of breach".
The US Secret Service said on Friday it is "working around the clock" with private sector partners "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds" stolen from Binance.

Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits.
Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury.
Binance, founded in China in 2017, lets users buy, sell and trade digital assets - it is estimated to have hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
Crypto is a digital asset, which doesn't exist physically and is instead accessed via digital wallets or computers.

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services. It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets”. sources.title: AI boom hits a wall on Wall Street as OpenAI cuts fundraising target while Meta gets a credit warning over its cash flow, spending and monetization - Yahoo Finance
passages: Quarterly earnings reports from hyperscalers this week spooked investors.
Alphabet saw its cash flow sink deeper into negative territory in the third quarter, with the Google parent also joining Meta and Amazon in charging ahead with massive spending plans.
On Thursday, Alphabet fell about 12%, its worst day on record.
The funding round was also upstaged by Anthropic, according to the report, as OpenAI's arch-rival prepares to go public next month.
Meanwhile, S&P sees Meta's capex reaching $140 billion this year, topping $225 billion in 2027, hitting $252 billion in 2028, and then flattening out from there.
At the same time, OpenAI was seeking more capital just as other AI giants tapped financial markets heavily.
This past week alone, Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing, Meta announced plans to raise $95 billion in equity, and Microsoft raised $25 billion in a bond sale.
Following a brutal selloff in tech stocks over the past week, OpenAI slashed the target on its latest fundraising round to $20 billion from $30 billion, sources told the Financial Times .
That also cut its expected valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion.

The prospect of hyperscalers continuing to hemorrhage funds was too much for S&P Global, which cut its outlook on Meta to "negative" from "stable" late Friday, citing negative cash flow and uncertainty around capital expenditure ​plans.
The credit ratings agency maintained Meta at AA- but warned ⁠the social media leader's leverage could top 1.0x as soon as 2027, which is the downgrade threshold for the current rating.
That's up from about 0.1x in 2025 and primarily reflects its strategy of leasing data center capacity rather than from its debt issuance.

The bearish environment on Wall Street also comes as rising bond yields have sent borrowing costs sharply higher, the political backlash against data centers is expected to help Democrats retake Congress, and the Iran war could re-escalate after midterm elections.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Microsoft reported strong cloud growth and stayed cash flow positive, though it said its capital spending will accelerate, while AI chip maker SK Hynix blew away earnings forecasts.

In a statement to Fortune , a Meta spokesperson said the company disagrees with S&P's assessment of its AI monetization capabilities, pointing to "significant product and business opportunities" ahead.
"Meta is already delivering stronger engagement, better recommendations, and greater returns for businesses as a result of AI investments," the spokesperson continued.

"We believe the technology and infrastructure we're building now will open new revenue streams, create long-term shareholder value, and bring us closer to delivering personal superintelligence to everyone."
Meta's rivals, however, are monetizing their data centers by leasing compute capacity, including to frontier model labs and enterprise customers, it added.
OpenAI didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The seemingly endless gusher of capital that's been showered on Silicon Valley during the AI boom may be coming to an end soon as Wall Street pushes back on massive spending plans. Following a brutal selloff in tech stocks over the past week, OpenAI slashed the target on its latest fundraising round to $20 billion from $30 billion, sources told the Financial Times . That also cut its expected valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion. The funding round was also upstaged by Anthropic, according to the report, as OpenAI's arch-rival prepares to go public next month. Ahead of its IPO, Anthropic filed an S-1 on Monday that showed revenue has soared and its cash flow turned positive in the first half of this year. OpenAI didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. The timing couldn't have been worse. Quarterly earnings reports from hyperscalers this week spooked investors. Alphabet saw its cash flow sink deeper into negative territory in the third quarter, with the Google parent also joining Meta and Amazon in charging ahead with massive spending plans. On Thursday, Alphabet fell about 12%, its worst day on record. To be sure, there were other positive signs as well, in addition to Anthropic's bullish S-1. Microsoft reported strong cloud growth and stayed cash flow positive, though it said its capital spending will accelerate, while AI chip maker SK Hynix blew away earnings forecasts. But the narrative had already turned bearish, especially after AI debt fears sent shares and bonds of "neocloud" companies tumbling earlier this month. At the same time, OpenAI was seeking more capital just as other AI giants tapped financial markets heavily. This past week alone, Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing, Meta announced plans to raise $95 billion in equity, and Microsoft raised $25 billion in a bond sale. The prospect of hyperscalers continuing to hemorrhage funds was too much for S&P Global, which cut its outlook on Meta to "negative" from "stable" late Friday, citing negative cash flow and uncertainty around capital expenditure ​plans. The credit ratings agency maintained Meta at AA- but warned ⁠the social media leader's leverage could top 1.0x as soon as 2027, which is the downgrade threshold for the current rating. That's up from about 0.1x in 2025 and primarily reflects its strategy of leasing data center capacity rather than from its debt issuance. Meanwhile, S&P sees Meta's capex reaching $140 billion this year, topping $225 billion in 2027, hitting $252 billion in 2028, and then flattening out from there. As a result, it expects free operating cash flow to remain negative: -$22 billion this year, -$71 billion in 2027, and -$39 billion in 2028. Of course, other hyperscalers are spending heavily and running cash deficits, but S&P also said Meta's ability to monetize its AI investments is more limited than that of its peers. "While we believe the company intends to monetize these investments via improved advertising tools that support faster ad revenue growth, as well as from the development of new revenue streams stemming from its introduction of agentic apps such as Muse, it is unclear when these revenue streams will generate material contributions that exceed their rising costs over the next few years," S&P said. Meta's rivals, however, are monetizing their data centers by leasing compute capacity, including to frontier model labs and enterprise customers, it added. In a statement to Fortune , a Meta spokesperson said the company disagrees with S&P's assessment of its AI monetization capabilities, pointing to "significant product and business opportunities" ahead. "Meta is already delivering stronger engagement, better recommendations, and greater returns for businesses as a result of AI investments," the spokesperson continued. "We believe the technology and infrastructure we're building now will open new revenue streams, create long-term shareholder value, and bring us closer to delivering personal superintelligence to everyone." The bearish environment on Wall Street also comes as rising bond yields have sent borrowing costs sharply higher, the political backlash against data centers is expected to help Democrats retake Congress, and the Iran war could re-escalate after midterm elections. Still, some bullish voices aren't convinced the AI boom is about to go bust, and even think some retrenchment is a good thing . According to market veteran Ed Yardeni, the AI investment boom faces financial, physical, and political constraints. If any of these constraints worsen, stocks could dive further, especially considering that AI is now a major driver of corporate earnings and GDP growth, he said in a note this week. "However, we view these constraints as healthy for the durability of the AI boom!" he added. For example, if the supply of capital doesn't flow as easily, it could lead to more efficient allocation, lowering the risk of overinvestment. Yardeni expects hyperscalers to retain access to financing—thanks to their strong balance sheets—and keep spending. In his view, it all comes down to the U.S. economy, which he said has performed remarkably well over the past few decades. Even the midterm elections are unlikely to derail it, regardless of which party controls Congress. "Further AI jitters therefore could set up buying opportunities rather than signal the end of the boom," he said. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

sources.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom

extraction.body: Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down. Over the past two weeks, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have outlined plans to spend more than $740 billion on capital expenditures this year, which Wall Street is reading as AI infrastructure spending, including data centers and chips. Earlier in the AI boom, investors largely rewarded such big outlays, viewing them as a sign of confidence in the technology’s growth potential. But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns. The anxiety spilled across the market on Friday. The Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and chip stocks took a drubbing, too: Nvidia dropped 4%, Broadcom more than 5%, and Qualcomm 11%. Alphabet, which plummeted 12% on Thursday, its worst day on record, wiping out $500 billion in market value, fell again. A big part of the concern is that companies that used to have overflowing free cash flow from their core businesses are getting hit as AI threatens the economics of those businesses. Alphabet provided the clearest example of that this week. Google’s parent company reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter, its second consecutive quarter in the red, even as quarterly capex grew to $51.4 billion. Alphabet expects to spend up to $205 billion this year, and expects that spending to keep rising in 2027. Meanwhile, the wild success of AI Mode — Google’s AI-powered chatbot feature built directly into Search — is eating into the company’s money-maker. Google’s Search advertising business, which makes up roughly half of its revenue, saw growth slow to 12%, its weakest pace in five quarters. That leaves Google walking a tightrope. It’s spending billions on the AI technology that could undermine the search business that pays it. passages: Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down.

Over the past two weeks, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have outlined plans to spend more than $740 billion on capital expenditures this year, which Wall Street is reading as AI infrastructure spending, including data centers and chips.

Earlier in the AI boom, investors largely rewarded such big outlays, viewing them as a sign of confidence in the technology’s growth potential. But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns.

The anxiety spilled across the market on Friday. The Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and chip stocks took a drubbing, too: Nvidia dropped 4%, Broadcom more than 5%, and Qualcomm 11%. Alphabet, which plummeted 12% on Thursday, its worst day on record, wiping out $500 billion in market value, fell again.

A big part of the concern is that companies that used to have overflowing free cash flow from their core businesses are getting hit as AI threatens the economics of those businesses. Alphabet provided the clearest example of that this week. Google’s parent company reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter, its second consecutive quarter in the red, even as quarterly capex grew to $51.4 billion. Alphabet expects to spend up to $205 billion this year, and expects that spending to keep rising in 2027.

Meanwhile, the wild success of AI Mode — Google’s AI-powered chatbot feature built directly into Search — is eating into the company’s money-maker. Google’s Search advertising business, which makes up roughly half of its revenue, saw growth slow to 12%, its weakest pace in five quarters. That leaves Google walking a tightrope. It’s spending billions on the AI technology that could undermine the search business that pays it.

As a result, shares of smaller companies that rent out AI computing power sank .

sources.title: Cracks emerge in AI borrowing boom as CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank debt worries grow - The Business Times
passages: The broader question is whether companies facing debt trouble like CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank are the industry’s weak links or are harbingers of deeper problems in the AI build-out.
Investors have sold off bonds for other AI giants as well, including Larry Ellison’s company, Oracle, though the price declines are not as steep as CoreWeave’s.
Not every data centre developer worries bond investors equally.
The larger so-called hyperscalers, such as Meta and Alphabet, which continue to borrow heavily, have been forced by investors to pay only modestly more in interest in recent debt deals.
The cost of insuring against losses on SoftBank’s debt has spiked.
It now costs more than US$40,000 to insure against US$1 million of SoftBank debt.
At the beginning of 2026, the cost was less than US$27,000.
Those questions burst into the forefront this past week when investors rapidly lost confidence in one debt-laden data centre company, CoreWeave.

Prices of its bonds – the company has accrued US$72 billion in liabilities to operate 51 data centres – crashed, and investors placed a more than 60 per cent likelihood that CoreWeave would fail to meet its obligations.
Oracle has faced slowdowns on multiple projects.
SoftBank has borrowed heavily to make one of the biggest bets – by dollar value – on OpenAI.
The Japanese conglomerate, led by Masayoshi Son, wrote its first US$500 million check in 2024 and a year later invested US$30 billion more.
That is just a year before Oracle’s debt comes due.
Some of the debt has traded around US$0.90 on the US dollar or below that, according to two traders, a steep drop for a relatively new loan.
CoreWeave’s business model defies easy description.
Its financial arrangements have been compared by some investors and analysts with those of the troubled office-space provider WeWork.
Oracle planned to pay back the borrowed money on the Texas facility helped by profits from the latter complex, called Project Lighthouse, which it expected to be operational by 2028.
In response to questions about SoftBank’s increasing debt, Alex Clavel, CEO of the SoftBank Vision Funds, said the amount of debt as a percentage of SoftBank Group’s assets had not changed.
TRILLIONS of dollars in borrowed money have powered the artificial intelligence boom.
First, CoreWeave buys Nvidia and other AI chips.
Then, as with WeWork, which leases space inside office buildings owned by others, CoreWeave contracts with data centre owners to use the structures for AI computing for 15 years or more.
CoreWeave then sub-leases the space to customers, including Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI, for a shorter time frame.
Several investors said they worried about whether hyperscalers like Meta and Microsoft would even need to lease space from CoreWeave in the future.
Alternately, they are wary of whether the data centres could become dated or even obsolete as their existing contracts expire.
Oracle faces similar permitting issues at a data centre project in New Mexico.
The project’s developer, investment firm Blue Owl, has started construction on the facility, but Oracle is struggling to get state permits to provide enough power.

The rub is that CoreWeave is on the hook for costs on both ends: It must pay to assemble and operate the facilities before any tenant is in place, and it is committed to the space for longer than its customers may stick around.

extraction.body: TRILLIONS of dollars in borrowed money have powered the artificial intelligence boom. But now there is growing uncertainty around just how easily more money can be obtained – and how much of it will be paid back. Those questions burst into the forefront this past week when investors rapidly lost confidence in one debt-laden data centre company, CoreWeave. Prices of its bonds – the company has accrued US$72 billion in liabilities to operate 51 data centres – crashed, and investors placed a more than 60 per cent likelihood that CoreWeave would fail to meet its obligations. Investors have sold off bonds for other AI giants as well, including Larry Ellison’s company, Oracle, though the price declines are not as steep as CoreWeave’s. At the same time, Wall Street investors have been bidding up the price of some complicated financial instruments that insure corporate debt against default, like those insuring SoftBank, the Japanese technology colossus that has borrowed heavily to bet its future on a partnership with OpenAI. The recent market moves could spell losses for investors that own the companies’ existing bonds and could mean the companies will be forced to pay higher interest rates when they borrow again, raising the costs of their already wildly expensive AI projects. The broader question is whether companies facing debt trouble like CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank are the industry’s weak links or are harbingers of deeper problems in the AI build-out. Five decades of milestones and moments that shaped Singapore’s success story - told through our headlines. The spread, or extra premium that investors demand to put their money into risky AI debt investments, has shot up more than 50 per cent over the past six months, according to Barclays, the investment bank. “The market is on a knife’s edge everywhere,” said Alexandra Coleman, founder of Azraq, a data centre risk researcher. A lot is riding on the continuation of the borrowing binge. Every week lately, economists, banks and private equity firms project higher and higher amounts of debt that they say will be needed to finance the AI systems that their boosters assert will run the world in a few years. Virtually every major mutual fund company, insurer and private equity firm has been buying up the AI debt, to say nothing of the scores of individual investors who have poured money into skyrocketing AI companies. Not every data centre developer worries bond investors equally. The larger so-called hyperscalers, such as Meta and Alphabet, which continue to borrow heavily, have been forced by investors to pay only modestly more in interest in recent debt deals. Investors have also sold out of some these companies’ existing debt, though the drop in bond prices has been less steep than for CoreWeave. CoreWeave’s business model defies easy description. Its financial arrangements have been compared by some investors and analysts with those of the troubled office-space provider WeWork. First, CoreWeave buys Nvidia and other AI chips. Then, as with WeWork, which leases space inside office buildings owned by others, CoreWeave contracts with data centre owners to use the structures for AI computing for 15 years or more. CoreWeave then sub-leases the space to customers, including Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI, for a shorter time frame. The rub is that CoreWeave is on the hook for costs on both ends: It must pay to assemble and operate the facilities before any tenant is in place, and it is committed to the space for longer than its customers may stick around. Several investors said they worried about whether hyperscalers like Meta and Microsoft would even need to lease space from CoreWeave in the future. Alternately, they are wary of whether the data centres could become dated or even obsolete as their existing contracts expire. A CoreWeave spokesperson, Lia Davis, said the company disagreed with the WeWork comparison. “The complexity of our financing reflects discipline, which is a point of pride for us,” she said in a statement. Another worry is the growing number of US data-centre projects being delayed by permitting issues or, in some cases, falling through. Oracle has faced slowdowns on multiple projects. In 2025, the company easily borrowed US$38 billion from a group of banks to build, with the help of project developers, a pair of data centres, one in Texas and another on about 809 hectares of farmland in Port Washington, Wisconsin. Oracle planned to pay back the borrowed money on the Texas facility helped by profits from the latter complex, called Project Lighthouse, which it expected to be operational by 2028. Aterio, a data centre researcher, said it was looking less likely that Project Lighthouse’s four data centres would start operating before 2029. That is just a year before Oracle’s debt comes due. Some of the debt has traded around US$0.90 on the US dollar or below that, according to two traders, a steep drop for a relatively new loan. Oracle faces similar permitting issues at a data centre project in New Mexico. The project’s developer, investment firm Blue Owl, has started construction on the facility, but Oracle is struggling to get state permits to provide enough power. Some of the US$18 billion in debt tied to the project has recently sold at steep discounts, roughly US$0.80 on the US dollar, according to two people familiar with the trades. SoftBank has borrowed heavily to make one of the biggest bets – by dollar value – on OpenAI. The Japanese conglomerate, led by Masayoshi Son, wrote its first US$500 million check in 2024 and a year later invested US$30 billion more. To get that money, Son sold off most of SoftBank’s holdings of Nvidia and T-Mobile and took out loans against his stake in chip designer Arm Holdings. In 2026, Son invested again. On Oct 1, SoftBank completed another US$30 billion investment in OpenAI. Before doing so, in late September the company raised a record US$11 billion in debt at interest rates of nearly 10 per cent. In response to questions about SoftBank’s increasing debt, Alex Clavel, CEO of the SoftBank Vision Funds, said the amount of debt as a percentage of SoftBank Group’s assets had not changed. “The assets we’ve owned have increased significantly,” Clavel said in an interview. The cost of insuring against losses on SoftBank’s debt has spiked. It now costs more than US$40,000 to insure against US$1 million of SoftBank debt. At the beginning of 2026, the cost was less than US$27,000. Some investors see a potential silver lining to the troubles. John Lloyd, the global head of multisector and corporate credit at asset manager Janus Henderson, said slowing down the financing for projects “makes existing projects and existing AI infrastructure even more valuable.” NYTIMES

The cost of insuring against losses on SoftBank’s debt has spiked. It now costs more than US$40,000 to insure against US$1 million of SoftBank debt. At the beginning of 2026, the cost was less than US$27,000.

Some investors see a potential silver lining to the troubles. John Lloyd, the global head of multisector and corporate credit at asset manager Janus Henderson, said slowing down the financing for projects “makes existing projects and existing AI infrastructure even more valuable.” NYTIMES

Microsoft reported strong cloud growth and stayed cash flow positive, though it said its capital spending will accelerate, while AI chip maker SK Hynix blew away earnings forecasts. But the narrative had already turned bearish, especially after AI debt fears sent shares and bonds of "neocloud" companies tumbling earlier this month. At the same time, OpenAI was seeking more capital just as other AI giants tapped financial markets heavily. This past week alone, Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing, Meta announced plans to raise $95 billion in equity, and Microsoft raised $25 billion in a bond sale. The credit ratings agency maintained Meta at AA- but warned ⁠the social media leader's leverage could top 1.0x as soon as 2027, which is the downgrade threshold for the current rating. That's up from about 0.1x in 2025 and primarily reflects its strategy of leasing data center capacity rather than from its debt issuance. Meanwhile, S&P sees Meta's capex reaching $140 billion this year, topping $225 billion in 2027, hitting $252 billion in 2028, and then flattening out from there. As a result, it expects free operating cash flow to remain negative: -$22 billion this year, -$71 billion in 2027, and -$39 billion in 2028. Of course, other hyperscalers are spending heavily and running cash deficits, but S&P also said Meta's ability to monetize its AI investments is more limited than that of its peers. "While we believe the company intends to monetize these investments via improved advertising tools that support faster ad revenue growth, as well as from the development of new revenue streams stemming from its introduction of agentic apps such as Muse, it is unclear when these revenue streams will generate material contributions that exceed their rising costs over the next few years," S&P said. Meta's rivals, however, are monetizing their data centers by leasing compute capacity, including to frontier model labs and enterprise customers, it added. In a statement to Fortune , a Meta spokesperson said the company disagrees with S&P's assessment of its AI monetization capabilities, pointing to "significant product and business opportunities" ahead. "Meta is already delivering stronger engagement, better recommendations, and greater returns for businesses as a result of AI investments," the spokesperson continued. "We believe the technology and infrastructure we're building now will open new revenue streams, create long-term shareholder value, and bring us closer to delivering personal superintelligence to everyone." The bearish environment on Wall Street also comes as rising bond yields have sent borrowing costs sharply higher, the political backlash against data centers is expected to help Democrats retake Congress, and the Iran war could re-escalate after midterm elections. Still, some bullish voices aren't convinced the AI boom is about to go bust, and even think some retrenchment is a good thing . According to market veteran Ed Yardeni, the AI investment boom faces financial, physical, and political constraints. If any of these constraints worsen, stocks could dive further, especially considering that AI is now a major driver of corporate earnings and GDP growth, he said in a note this week. "However, we view these constraints as healthy for the durability of the AI boom!" he added. For example, if the supply of capital doesn't flow as easily, it could lead to more efficient allocation, lowering the risk of overinvestment. Yardeni expects hyperscalers to retain access to financing—thanks to their strong balance sheets—and keep spending. In his view, it all comes down to the U.S. economy, which he said has performed remarkably well over the past few decades. Even the midterm elections are unlikely to derail it, regardless of which party controls Congress. "Further AI jitters therefore could set up buying opportunities rather than signal the end of the boom," he said. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

sources.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom

extraction.body: Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down. Over the past two weeks, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have outlined plans to spend more than $740 billion on capital expenditures this year, which Wall Street is reading as AI infrastructure spending, including data centers and chips. Earlier in the AI boom, investors largely rewarded such big outlays, viewing them as a sign of confidence in the technology’s growth potential. But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns. The anxiety spilled across the market on Friday. The Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and chip stocks took a drubbing, too: Nvidia dropped 4%, Broadcom more than 5%, and Qualcomm 11%. Alphabet, which plummeted 12% on Thursday, its worst day on record, wiping out $500 billion in market value, fell again. A big part of the concern is that companies that used to have overflowing free cash flow from their core businesses are getting hit as AI threatens the economics of those businesses. Alphabet provided the clearest example of that this week. Google’s parent company reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter, its second consecutive quarter in the red, even as quarterly capex grew to $51.4 billion. Alphabet expects to spend up to $205 billion this year, and expects that spending to keep rising in 2027. Meanwhile, the wild success of AI Mode — Google’s AI-powered chatbot feature built directly into Search — is eating into the company’s money-maker. Google’s Search advertising business, which makes up roughly half of its revenue, saw growth slow to 12%, its weakest pace in five quarters. That leaves Google walking a tightrope. It’s spending billions on the AI technology that could undermine the search business that pays it. Amazon is in a similar boat after reporting negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the past 12 months, compared with $14.8 billion in positive free cash flow the year before. The company says it expects to spend $220 billion in capex this year. Even though revenue at its cloud business, AWS, grew 39%, Amazon’s stock tumbled 7% after it reported earnings Thursday. Meta is also burning cash, reporting negative free cash flow of $2.1 billion in the third quarter as capex outpaced its operating cash. It’s guiding to as much as $145 billion in capex this year. The company noted that Muse, its new free personal AI agent, is a bit of a money pit (it’s “very compute-intensive to run,” CEO Mark Zuckerberg has said). But ad revenue grew 26%. Still, no amount of good news saved Meta from taking a 10% hit on its stock last week. Microsoft was the only exception when it came to free cash flow — it recorded $18.6 billion in positive free cash flow in its latest quarter, with spending on capex at $45.2 billion, less than the $50 billion it projected. Microsoft said that wasn’t an intentional pullback from AI spending, blaming delays in capacity from third-party providers. As a result, shares of smaller companies that rent out AI computing power sank . It’s worth noting that the money to pay for all of this AI infrastructure isn’t just coming from the Big Tech companies’ profits. It’s also showing up in stock and bond sales. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle raised a combined $326 billion in debt in 2026, triple the amount raised last year. Demand for AI compute remains strong. Google, Amazon, and Microsoft all saw gains in their cloud businesses. But investors are getting spooked by the costs of meeting that demand. These muddied waters could complicate Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO. The AI company filed to go public earlier this week, and its future growth depends on securing enormous amounts of compute. Financial Times reported Friday that Blackstone has warned investors the company might not qualify for an investment-grade rating after its IPO, meaning it might end up being more reliant on the hyperscalers and third-parties to fund its infrastructure ambitions. Rebecca Bellan is a senior reporter at TechCrunch where she covers the business, policy, and emerging trends shaping artificial intelligence. Her work has also appeared in Forbes, Bloomberg, The Atlantic, The Daily Beast, and other publications. The company is investing heavily in AI technology that could put pressure on the search business funding that investment.

The market reaction was swift. The Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Friday. Nvidia dropped 4%, Broadcom fell more than 5% and Qualcomm declined 11%. Alphabet, after plunging 12% on Thursday in its worst day on record and losing $500 billion in market value, fell again.

Amazon reported negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the past 12 months, compared with positive free cash flow of $14.8 billion in the prior year. The company expects capital spending of $220 billion this year.

Its cloud business, AWS, grew revenue 39%. Still, Amazon shares fell 7% after the company reported earnings Thursday. The contrast captures the tension facing investors: demand for cloud computing is growing, but the infrastructure needed to serve it carries a steep bill.

Meta also reported negative free cash flow, at $2.1 billion in the third quarter, as capital spending exceeded operating cash. The company is guiding for as much as $145 billion in capital spending this year. Its ad revenue grew 26%, but Meta shares still lost 10% last week.

Meta has described Muse, its new free personal AI agent, as expensive to operate. Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg said it is “very compute-intensive to run.” That makes the investment question more direct: even a popular AI feature can add substantial computing costs, while the company still depends on advertising revenue.

Microsoft was the only one of the four to report positive free cash flow in its latest quarter, recording $18.6 billion. Capital spending came to $45.2 billion, below the $50 billion the company had projected.

Microsoft said the lower figure did not reflect a deliberate retreat from AI investment. It blamed delays in capacity from third-party providers, a development that also sent shares of smaller companies renting out AI computing power lower.

The spending boom is also being financed through borrowing and securities sales, not only through profits. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle raised a combined $326 billion in debt in 2026, triple the amount raised last year, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Demand for AI computing remains strong, and Google, Amazon and Microsoft all recorded gains in their cloud businesses. The pressure falls on whether those gains can justify the cost of meeting demand. For investors, that question now sits alongside the companies’ latest cash-flow figures and spending plans.

sources.title: Cracks emerge in AI borrowing boom as CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank debt worries grow - The Business Times
passages: The broader question is whether companies facing debt trouble like CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank are the industry’s weak links or are harbingers of deeper problems in the AI build-out.
Investors have sold off bonds for other AI giants as well, including Larry Ellison’s company, Oracle, though the price declines are not as steep as CoreWeave’s.
Not every data centre developer worries bond investors equally.
The larger so-called hyperscalers, such as Meta and Alphabet, which continue to borrow heavily, have been forced by investors to pay only modestly more in interest in recent debt deals.
The cost of insuring against losses on SoftBank’s debt has spiked.
It now costs more than US$40,000 to insure against US$1 million of SoftBank debt.
At the beginning of 2026, the cost was less than US$27,000.
Those questions burst into the forefront this past week when investors rapidly lost confidence in one debt-laden data centre company, CoreWeave.

Prices of its bonds – the company has accrued US$72 billion in liabilities to operate 51 data centres – crashed, and investors placed a more than 60 per cent likelihood that CoreWeave would fail to meet its obligations.
Oracle has faced slowdowns on multiple projects.
SoftBank has borrowed heavily to make one of the biggest bets – by dollar value – on OpenAI.
The Japanese conglomerate, led by Masayoshi Son, wrote its first US$500 million check in 2024 and a year later invested US$30 billion more.
That is just a year before Oracle’s debt comes due.
Some of the debt has traded around US$0.90 on the US dollar or below that, according to two traders, a steep drop for a relatively new loan.
CoreWeave’s business model defies easy description.
Its financial arrangements have been compared by some investors and analysts with those of the troubled office-space provider WeWork.
Oracle planned to pay back the borrowed money on the Texas facility helped by profits from the latter complex, called Project Lighthouse, which it expected to be operational by 2028.
In response to questions about SoftBank’s increasing debt, Alex Clavel, CEO of the SoftBank Vision Funds, said the amount of debt as a percentage of SoftBank Group’s assets had not changed.
TRILLIONS of dollars in borrowed money have powered the artificial intelligence boom.
First, CoreWeave buys Nvidia and other AI chips.
Then, as with WeWork, which leases space inside office buildings owned by others, CoreWeave contracts with data centre owners to use the structures for AI computing for 15 years or more.
CoreWeave then sub-leases the space to customers, including Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI, for a shorter time frame.
Several investors said they worried about whether hyperscalers like Meta and Microsoft would even need to lease space from CoreWeave in the future.
Alternately, they are wary of whether the data centres could become dated or even obsolete as their existing contracts expire.
Oracle faces similar permitting issues at a data centre project in New Mexico.
The project’s developer, investment firm Blue Owl, has started construction on the facility, but Oracle is struggling to get state permits to provide enough power.

The rub is that CoreWeave is on the hook for costs on both ends: It must pay to assemble and operate the facilities before any tenant is in place, and it is committed to the space for longer than its customers may stick around.
