Rezaei says US tone shifted to a positive, more conciliatory stance. Iranian foreign minister Araghchi calls Vance letter a positive step toward dialogue.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the tone of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance had “changed completely,” describing it as a positive development as Tehran awaited Washington’s response. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera that “The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and understanding more broadly is a positive step,” while also saying Tehran was not yet ready for direct negotiations with American officials. Iran’s remarks came as mediators intensified efforts to avert renewed strikes, with the diplomatic push involving Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries and consultations that included talks in Tehran and then shifted to Doha.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump had not made a decision on further strikes and that the administration remained open to a diplomatic solution. Rezaei did not disclose the contents of Vance’s letter, and Araghchi said Tehran was reviewing proposals concerning its nuclear programme.

At the 22nd IISS Manama Dialogue in Bahrain, GCC Secretary General Jasem Mohamed Al Budaiwi said the GCC states “still do” call for dialogue and negotiation to resolve issues in the region. Al Budaiwi added that “But diplomacy needs partners, partners who respond in kind,” and he said the six-member bloc maintained open channels with Iran alongside partnerships with Western powers, China, Russia and other countries. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty warned that “The second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere,” and he said military action could unleash consequences beyond the control of those who initiated it.

Al Budaiwi called for navigation through the Strait of Hormuz to return to conditions before February 28, when the US-Iran war began, and he said disruptions to the strait had affected energy prices, shipping, insurance and global supply chains. Britain’s Middle East Minister Stephen Doughty said the UK had deployed air defense equipment and personnel to Saudi Arabia and that “We must strain every sinew for peace,” while promising continued diplomatic engagement.

Iran’s position remained that the shift in Washington’s tone did not remove its conditions, and Mohsen Rezaei said in a video broadcast on Iranian television that “Their tone has completely changed,” while he said he “haven’t yet responded.” Araghchi told Al Jazeera that Tehran had studied the letter in high-level meetings and warned that if Washington’s objective was to “foment discord,” it would be “one more mistake to add to the previous ones.” Araghchi also said Tehran had “no plans to meet with American officials,” and he described circulating claims about such meetings as “mere media speculation.”

In parallel, mediators continued consultations on Iran’s conditions, and Araghchi said his aides were in Qatar while mediators in Qatar and Pakistan continued their consultations on those conditions. The diplomatic opening left unresolved disagreements over nuclear and sanctions issues, with Washington seeking nuclear concessions from Tehran while Iran sought relief from the US naval blockade, access to frozen funds and permission to resume oil sales.

extraction.body: The startup maps how identities, assets and vulnerabilities connect, and uses AI agents to find and fix risky combinations of issues. Northstar Security, a startup developing AI agents for security teams, has emerged from stealth mode with $7 million in seed funding. Wing Venture Capital led the round. MVP, Outliers, and cybersecurity veterans Gerhard Eschelbeck, Renaud Deraison, and Justin Somaini also invested. The company ingests data from existing security and IT tools to build what it calls a Security Context Graph. Updated in real time, the graph shows how identities, assets, applications, vulnerabilities, and business systems connect to one another. Northstar aims to catch so-called toxic combinations. Issues such as a vulnerability, an unmanaged device, or an account with excessive privileges may seem under control on their own, but together they can expose critical business systems. For instance, the platform could flag a laptop lacking endpoint protection whose owner is a privileged user able to reach a critical payroll system. Analysts can investigate findings like this by asking questions in plain language. Northstar’s agents can then kick off fixes, such as installing endpoint protection, notifying the user, or limiting their access, and people can supervise those actions where appropriate. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading. Customers can also give external AI agents access to the graph through Model Context Protocol (MCP) and build their own security workflows. Northstar says it connects to more than 70 enterprise security and IT products, among them Okta, GitHub, Workday, Microsoft Defender and Entra, AWS, and Google Cloud. “Security teams are drowning in data but starving for context,” said Amer Deeba, Northstar’s CEO and co-founder. Deeba co-founded Normalyze, which Proofpoint later acquired , and was previously a senior executive at Qualys. His co-founder, CTO Ed Rowe, held the same role at Farmers Business Network and led engineering as an SVP at AppDynamics. The startup will use the money to develop its platform, hire staff, and expand its go-to-market push. extraction.body: On Thursday evening, I slipped on my neon yellow heels and a floral mini dress. It’s New York, so I can wear whatever I want to a midterm election event full of media types, techies, policy advocates, and, well, does anyone else even exist at these things? I walked into the dimly blue-lit Brooklyn warehouse and was surprised to see the room already filling up. Newsreel, the media company founded by former Forbes and Newsweek reporter Jack Brewster, hosted the event, and the lineup was heavy-hitting. Kenneth Schlenker, co-founder of the focus app Opal, sat down for a fireside chat about “the state of attention,” and Aryan Banjan, who built the campaign management software Barza, gave a midterm forecast. I, meanwhile, was moderating a panel on data centers. Brewster said the goal was for people to “put their phones away and talk to each other about the election, five days out.” As the evening progressed, however, one topic consumed nearly every conversation: AI, data centers, and the backlash against the growing technocracy. Lately, as a tech reporter, I’ve noticed a growing chasm between tech and everyone else. I spend most of my days talking to people who see the benefits of AI, who are so ambitious in building it and so optimistic that it will succeed that, when I talk to people beyond the tech world, I forget how ugly it all seems to them. Outside the tech bubble, data centers and AI have become such an intense ballot-box issue that they could sway some midterm races on November 3. A recent report from Data Center Watch found that almost $200 billion in data center projects were delayed, stalled, or blocked in the first half of 2026 due to political and community opposition. Meanwhile, states like Pennsylvania, Georgia, Texas, New York, and Virginia are considering more guardrails and transparency around data centers’ rapid development. Hundreds of new data centers are planned in Virginia alone, a state already nicknamed the “data center capital of the world.” A fireside chat with New York City Council member Chi Ossé, just before my panel, set the tone. AI came up near the end; Ossé said he doesn’t really use it. To me, though, he didn’t seem to be for or against it. He mostly emphasized that he would like to see tech executives held more accountable and trillionaires like Elon Musk taxed more. He described himself as a democratic socialist, but a “law and order” one. When CEOs talk about a technology that could deplete 10% of human civilization, he said, “they should be called to testify in front of Congress.” My panel was up next. I moderated a discussion with Maia Woluchem, a technology and human rights researcher, and Hilary Flint, an environmental and public health advocate, about data centers. As I took the stage, I decided to get a better read on the crowd. I asked, “Who here is pro-AI data center?” and was promptly booed. Our conversation covered a range of topics and emotions. People are upset that big tech companies appear to be cutting secret deals with local officials to build billion-dollar data centers. In some cases, zoning rules make it unclear what is being built until it’s too late to protest. At the same time, people are struggling with the cost of living and doing everything they can to hold onto what’s left of the American Dream, while tech leaders talk about AI replacing workers, or even humanity itself. extraction.body: Vic Mensa is one of those people who has done so many things that it’s hard to remember where you were first introduced to him. Or maybe his house-influenced single “Down On My Luck”? Maybe you didn’t even realize that Mensa was a rapper. Or perhaps you’re mostly aware of him through his activism, social media presence (peeling oranges and waxing poetic), or his podcast The Vic Mensa Show. Part of the secret to being so prolific, it turns out, is Voice Memos. Songs, essay ideas, orange tree thoughts, voice notes to myself at some wild hour, little things my son says that I do not want to lose. My phone is a million distractions in one rectangle, but Voice Memos is one of the few parts of it that still feels honest. That’s definitely where my voice has really found its legs. I started out peeling an orange and talking through whatever was on my mind, and it turned into this whole conversation with people about politics, history, music, grief, jokes, fatherhood, all of it. That response helped show me there was room for The Vic Mensa Show too. What is the last GIF or meme you used? [Image: Ummm… that is not Vic Mensa.

passages: THE LOWDOWN Arsenal welcome Aston Villa to Emirates Stadium on Sunday at 12noon in the WSL.
LAST TIME OUT When the teams last met in May at Villa Park, Arsenal ran out 3-0 winners with a brace from Russo and a goal from Frida Maanum.
In this fixture at the Emirates last season, Frida Maanum’s early goal was cancelled out by a stoppage time equaliser from Paula Tomas.
‘Very often it happens that teams do something different against us.
We have to focus on ourselves and keep building on our last performance.
The Gunners will want to continue to ride the wave they have just about clambered onto and water the green shoots of confidence and vivacity we saw on Wednesday.
A WORD FROM THE BOSS ‘Knowing from his (Villa manager Brian Sorensen) Everton team, I think it was always hard to play against Natalia [Arroyo]’s Aston Villa team as well.
Arsenal lose Dowman appeal as three-match ban upheld
While the victory at Spurs was won with gritted teeth and matted hair, Wednesday night’s performance against Benfica was far more fluent and finessed.
Arsenal simply have to go on a good run now having surrendered so many points already this season and they have to take the energy and enthusiasm of the last two games into this encounter.
Alessia Russo bagged the winner at Spurs and helped herself to a Champions League hat-trick on Wednesday, she is fast becoming Arsenal’s ‘franchise player’ if she isn’t already.
It will be interesting to see how far Slegers sticks with some of these burgeoning stabilisers on Sunday.

Arsenal also needed leadership to guide them out of their rough patch and Foord’s unwavering commitment and willingness to compete for duels has given Arsenal an injection of intensity at a time when confidence was sagging.
Sometimes you have to punch your way out of a rut and few players swing like Caitlin.

Renee Slegers’ side earned back-to-back victories for the first time this season with a 2-1 win over Spurs in the North London derby followed by a consummate 3-0 victory over Benfica in the Champions League on Wednesday night. While the victory at Spurs was won with gritted teeth and matted hair, Wednesday night’s performance against Benfica was far more fluent and finessed. Arsenal simply have to go on a good run now having surrendered so many points already this season and they have to take the energy and enthusiasm of the last two games into this encounter. Last season, Villa came to the Emirates and forced one of Arsenal’s six damaging league draws with a late equaliser after an insipid display. The Gunners will want to continue to ride the wave they have just about clambered onto and water the green shoots of confidence and vivacity we saw on Wednesday. Alessia Russo bagged the winner at Spurs and helped herself to a Champions League hat-trick on Wednesday, she is fast becoming Arsenal’s ‘franchise player’ if she isn’t already. A front two of Smith and Russo has shown some positive signs in the last two games, with Hinds and Foord stablising the left side of the team. It will be interesting to see how far Slegers sticks with some of these burgeoning stabilisers on Sunday. Available squad Goalkeepers: 16.Misa 28.Borbe 40.Damm Defenders: 2.Fox 3.Wubben-Moy 5.De Almeida 6.Williamson 7.Catley 22.O.Batlle 24.Hinds 31.Holmberg Midfielders: 4.Stanway 10.Little 12.L.Maanum 14.Reuteler 32.Cooney-Cross Forwards: 9.Foord 11.Smith 19.Baum 23.Russo 25.Blackstenius Unavailable: 1.van Domselaar 8.Mariona 17.Agyemang 18.Kelly 26.Reid 29.Cerci A WORD FROM THE BOSS ‘Knowing from his (Villa manager Brian Sorensen) Everton team, I think it was always hard to play against Natalia [Arroyo]’s Aston Villa team as well. They would pose a lot of questions. Now, of course, with Brian, they’ve had a really good start. I think it’s four wins and a draw. They won last night through penalties. ‘We remember the game last year, how it was difficult at Emirates for us at home. The away game was good, it was dominant. We have to be prepared, we have to be humble. What they’re going to do, it’s always a guessing game. Of course, they’re in a transition now and they’ve changed their system. Let’s see what they do against us. ‘Very often it happens that teams do something different against us. Let’s see what their game plan is. We have to focus on ourselves and keep building on our last performance. It’s good, it’s two good wins. It was Arsenal, this was us last night, and now we have to back it up with the next game coming up against Villa.’ LAST TIME OUT When the teams last met in May at Villa Park, Arsenal ran out 3-0 winners with a brace from Russo and a goal from Frida Maanum. In this fixture at the Emirates last season, Frida Maanum’s early goal was cancelled out by a stoppage time equaliser from Paula Tomas. THE OPPOSITION After an underwhelming start to the season, Spanish coach Natalia Arroyo was sacked at the end of September having lost two and drawn two of their opening four games (though one of their draws was at Stamford Bridge). Former Everton manager Brian Sorensen had been installed as Villa’s Technical Director last season and has taken the role on an interim basis until the end of the season. Villa are unbeaten since Sorensen took over; they have drawn with Crystal Palace but beaten Liverpool and Everton, as well as notching a Subway Player’s Cup win against Burnley and, on Wednesday night, they beat Birmingham on penalties in the same competition. While not sparkling yet, their form has corrected. Villa have moved to a 3421 formation that Sorensen often deployed at Everton with Wilms and Maritz as wing-backs, allowing Chastity Grant to push up the pitch. Sorensen’s teams tend to like to possess the ball, draw the press and then quickly play in behind to pacy wide forwards. Caitlin Foord won Player of the Match in last weekend’s North London Derby and also played very well in Wednesday’s game against Benfica. Her partnership with Taylor Hinds on the left hand side has brought greater defensive security. Caitlin’s qualities have also provided a nice blend with Smith as a centre-forward and Russo in behind. Arsenal also needed leadership to guide them out of their rough patch and Foord’s unwavering commitment and willingness to compete for duels has given Arsenal an injection of intensity at a time when confidence was sagging. Sometimes you have to punch your way out of a rut and few players swing like Caitlin. Slegers was full of praise for Foord in her pre-match press conference too , ‘The way she plays is contagious and she’s been so important for us in that game and with that performance and everything she brought and everything we expected, we needed against Benfica, because we expected a fight there as well. We wanted her to be on a pitch again and she had a great 90 minutes again for us.’ COMING UP Sunday • Line-ups posted an hour before kickoff • Aidan Gibson’s on the whistle match report • Every word of Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference • Opinion piece from the game Monday • Arsenal Women Arsecast with Tim and Jamie analysing the game • Potentially a tactical analysis piece Don’t forget to sign up for our free Arsenal Women Weekly Newsletter . Her sheer bloody minded tenacity is the why. After letting go of McCabe and Mead we had to retain a couple of gutsy players in the squad to help us through this poor start. If Villa play a low block it will be very interesting to see how we get on against it given our upturn in results. I guess it could go one of two ways. We struggle, confidence drains and we have a set back. Or we do well and it’s a further boost to confidence. Let’s hope it’s the latter. I don’t think Villa are a low block type of team. They have often caused us trouble in the past at our own end never mind our target end. They have also had their fair share of ex-Gunners too so it’s good to see how the likes of Anna Patten and Noelle Maritz are getting on. After the much improved performance on Wednesday night, let’s hope this leads to a resounding victory tomorrow.

They would pose a lot of questions. Now, of course, with Brian, they’ve had a really good start. I think it’s four wins and a draw. They won last night through penalties.

‘We remember the game last year, how it was difficult at Emirates for us at home. The away game was good, it was dominant. We have to be prepared, we have to be humble. What they’re going to do, it’s always a guessing game. Of course, they’re in a transition now and they’ve changed their system. Let’s see what they do against us.

‘Very often it happens that teams do something different against us. Let’s see what their game plan is. We have to focus on ourselves and keep building on our last performance. It’s good, it’s two good wins. It was Arsenal, this was us last night, and now we have to back it up with the next game coming up against Villa.’

LAST TIME OUT When the teams last met in May at Villa Park, Arsenal ran out 3-0 winners with a brace from Russo and a goal from Frida Maanum. In this fixture at the Emirates last season, Frida Maanum’s early goal was cancelled out by a stoppage time equaliser from Paula Tomas.

THE OPPOSITION After an underwhelming start to the season, Spanish coach Natalia Arroyo was sacked at the end of September having lost two and drawn two of their opening four games (though one of their draws was at Stamford Bridge). Former Everton manager Brian Sorensen had been installed as Villa’s Technical Director last season and has taken the role on an interim basis until the end of the season.

Villa are unbeaten since Sorensen took over; they have drawn with Crystal Palace but beaten Liverpool and Everton, as well as notching a Subway Player’s Cup win against Burnley and, on Wednesday night, they beat Birmingham on penalties in the same competition. While not sparkling yet, their form has corrected.

Villa have moved to a 3421 formation that Sorensen often deployed at Everton with Wilms and Maritz as wing-backs, allowing Chastity Grant to push up the pitch. Sorensen’s teams tend to like to possess the ball, draw the press and then quickly play in behind to pacy wide forwards.

Caitlin Foord won Player of the Match in last weekend’s North London Derby and also played very well in Wednesday’s game against Benfica. Her partnership with Taylor Hinds on the left hand side has brought greater defensive security. Caitlin’s qualities have also provided a nice blend with Smith as a centre-forward and Russo in behind.

Arsenal also needed leadership to guide them out of their rough patch and Foord’s unwavering commitment and willingness to compete for duels has given Arsenal an injection of intensity at a time when confidence was sagging. Sometimes you have to punch your way out of a rut and few players swing like Caitlin.

Slegers was full of praise for Foord in her pre-match press conference too , ‘The way she plays is contagious and she’s been so important for us in that game and with that performance and everything she brought and everything we expected, we needed against Benfica, because we expected a fight there as well. We wanted her to be on a pitch again and she had a great 90 minutes again for us.’

Her sheer bloody minded tenacity is the why. After letting go of McCabe and Mead we had to retain a couple of gutsy players in the squad to help us through this poor start.

If Villa play a low block it will be very interesting to see how we get on against it given our upturn in results. I guess it could go one of two ways. We struggle, confidence drains and we have a set back. Or we do well and it’s a further boost to confidence. Let’s hope it’s the latter.

I don’t think Villa are a low block type of team. They have often caused us trouble in the past at our own end never mind our target end. They have also had their fair share of ex-Gunners too so it’s good to see how the likes of Anna Patten and Noelle Maritz are getting on.
After the much improved performance on Wednesday night, let’s hope this leads to a resounding victory tomorrow.

LAST TIME OUT When the teams last met in May at Villa Park, Arsenal ran out 3-0 winners with a brace from Russo and a goal from Frida Maanum.
In this fixture at the Emirates last season, Frida Maanum’s early goal was cancelled out by a stoppage time equaliser from Paula Tomas.
‘Very often it happens that teams do something different against us.
We have to focus on ourselves and keep building on our last performance.
The Gunners will want to continue to ride the wave they have just about clambered onto and water the green shoots of confidence and vivacity we saw on Wednesday.
A WORD FROM THE BOSS ‘Knowing from his (Villa manager Brian Sorensen) Everton team, I think it was always hard to play against Natalia [Arroyo]’s Aston Villa team as well.
Arsenal lose Dowman appeal as three-match ban upheld
While the victory at Spurs was won with gritted teeth and matted hair, Wednesday night’s performance against Benfica was far more fluent and finessed.
Arsenal simply have to go on a good run now having surrendered so many points already this season and they have to take the energy and enthusiasm of the last two games into this encounter.
Alessia Russo bagged the winner at Spurs and helped herself to a Champions League hat-trick on Wednesday, she is fast becoming Arsenal’s ‘franchise player’ if she isn’t already.
It will be interesting to see how far Slegers sticks with some of these burgeoning stabilisers on Sunday.

Arsenal also needed leadership to guide them out of their rough patch and Foord’s unwavering commitment and willingness to compete for duels has given Arsenal an injection of intensity at a time when confidence was sagging.
Sometimes you have to punch your way out of a rut and few players swing like Caitlin.

extraction.body: The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon takes place on Sunday, November 1, bringing nearly 60,000 runners from around the world to the streets of New York for one of the most iconic races on the international running calendar. The professional women’s race is scheduled to start at 8:35 a.m. Follow this live results guide for real-time updates on the men’s and women’s winners, finishing times, podium finishers and official standings. The winners of the 2026 New York City Marathon have not yet been confirmed. The men’s and women’s results tables below will be updated in real time as the competition unfolds, with the official champions, finishing times and final standings added once they are verified. The results will be updated throughout race day as athletes cross the finish line. Final positions and finishing times will be checked against the official New York Road Runners results. Follow the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon as the elite runners compete across Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan. For live runner tracking, visit NYRR Live Results. For verified finishing times and final standings, check the official NYRR results portal. He will try to become the first men’s runner since John Kagwe in 1998 to win consecutive New York City Marathon titles. European interest centers on the Netherlands’ Abdi Nageeye (2:04:20) and Sweden’s Andreas Almgren, who is making his marathon debut after establishing himself on the track and in the half marathon. Kenya’s Hellen Obiri is the leading name in the women’s competition. She returns after winning in 2023 and 2025, when she set the course record of 2:19:51. Her main challengers include compatriots Sheila Chepkirui, the 2024 champion with a personal best of 2:17:19, and Viola Cheptoo (2:19:05). Ethiopia’s Gotytom Gebreslase (2:18:11) and American runner Jessica McClain (2:22:43) are also among the names to watch. These are pre-race contenders, not confirmed 2026 winners. The final positions and times will be published only after they are verified. The race takes place on Sunday, November 1, with professional and mass-participation divisions starting at different times. The 2026 race falls on the same day that daylight saving time ends in the United States. Clocks move back one hour at 2:00 a.m., so New York will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST) when the marathon begins. The New York Road Runners (NYRR), the race organizer, provides the official results and runner-tracking services. The men’s and women’s champions, finishing times and final podium positions will be added to this article as the official information becomes available.

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, WWD may receive an affiliate commission. It goes without saying that the annual New York City Marathon is one of the most special days of the year: uniting strangers, both spectators and runners alike, in the pursuit of 26.2 miles. Traditionally taking place on the first Sunday of November, this year’s TCS New York City Marathon lands on November 1, kicking off at 8:00 a.m. EST for the professional wheelchair and handcycle divisions, with the pros assembling at the starting line next — followed by five waves of amateur runners. Related Articles Shoe Industry News Jimmy Choo Momentum Grows as Shoes Reclaim the Fashion Spotlight Fashion The Art of Gifting Well: 21 Luxury Christmas Gifts for Men Who Appreciate the Finer Things Weaving its way through all five of the city’s boroughs, the marathon’s route has been adjusted for the first time in 15 years (the change affects a portion of the course in the South Bronx). 2026 also marks the 50th anniversary of said five-borough concept, as the marathon was originally based only in Central Park before expanding, and drawing in more participants, to celebrate the U.S. Bicentennial. If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. It will be broadcast on WABC-TV locally and on ESPN2 nationally; cable cutters, though, can tune in with the help of a few editor-recommended streaming platforms like DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay. – Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost. – Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed. – $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor. According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.” Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir. Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park. Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31. At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. He had the Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 shoe on, which was also spotted on winners’ feet at marathons across Tokyo, London, Berlin, and Chicago last year. New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99. Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release. Related Articles Shoe Industry News Jimmy Choo Momentum Grows as Shoes Reclaim the Fashion Spotlight Fashion The Art of Gifting Well: 21 Luxury Christmas Gifts for Men Who Appreciate the Finer Things

Weaving its way through all five of the city’s boroughs, the marathon’s route has been adjusted for the first time in 15 years (the change affects a portion of the course in the South Bronx). 2026 also marks the 50th anniversary of said five-borough concept, as the marathon was originally based only in Central Park before expanding, and drawing in more participants, to celebrate the U.S. Bicentennial.

If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. It will be broadcast on WABC-TV locally and on ESPN2 nationally; cable cutters, though, can tune in with the help of a few editor-recommended streaming platforms like DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay.
– Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels

ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost.
– Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels

Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed.
– $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels

Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor.

According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.”

Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir.

Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park.

Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31.

At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. He had the Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 shoe on, which was also spotted on winners’ feet at marathons across Tokyo, London, Berlin, and Chicago last year.

New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99.

Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release.
Get inspired by the best of the best in running — and their sneaker choices — by watching the New York City Marathon on November 1, courtesy of DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV .

extraction.body: On Sunday, November 1, nearly 60,000 runners taking on the New York City Marathon will get the rare privilege of having city traffic stop for them as they cover 26.2 miles through the five boroughs. And with coverage stretching from early morning into Sunday night, you don't necessarily have to be standing along First Avenue or waiting near Central Park to catch everyone in action.Here's what you need to know about watching the race, including start times, broadcasts, and how to follow individual runners.What Time Does the 2026 NYC Marathon Start?Things get going at 8 a.m. Handcycles and select athletes with disabilities start at 8:22 a.m., before the professional women take off at 8:35 a.m. and the men follow at 9:05 a.m.The rest of the field will leave Staten Island in five waves, beginning at 9:10 a.m. and continuing through 11:30 a.m.How to Watch the 2026 NYC MarathonThe main national broadcast starts at 8 a.m. ET on ESPN2, with coverage running until 11:30 a.m. If you'd rather stream, the ESPN app has the same coverage with an ESPN Unlimited plan, plus an extra hour of prerace programming beginning at 7 a.m. and more action through 1 p.m. There's a Spanish-language feed during the main 8 to 11:30 a.m. window as well.In New York and the surrounding tri-state area, ABC7/WABC-TV is another option. Coverage begins at 7 a.m., ahead of the race broadcast from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., which you can also stream on the ABC 7 New York app.For anyone more interested in the finish line than the rest of the course, ABC7NY.com and the ABC 7 New York app have you covered from 10:30 a.m. until 6 p.m. with a dedicated live stream. That should give you plenty of time to catch the professionals and stick around for the thousands of other runners making their way into Central Park.ABC also has a national Live from the TCS New York City Marathon special scheduled for 3 to 5 p.m. Before hopping on the subway, you'll probably want to check how far along they are, which is where the official New York Road Runners app comes in handy.You can track individual runners throughout the race, check their progress at timing points, and pull up leaderboards and results. The app is available for iOS and Android, and it also has live feeds for each of the four professional races if you want to keep an eye on the elites while you're out cheering.Who to Watch at the 2026 NYC MarathonLast year's champions, Benson Kipruto and Hellen Obiri, are both coming back, and each has a memorable performance to defend. Kipruto won the closest men's finish in NYC Marathon history in 2025, while Obiri ran 2:19:51 to break the women's course record that had stood for 22 years.Conner Mantz and Zouhair Talbi are among the Americans to watch in the men's race. On the women's side, Weini Kelati is making her marathon debut against a field that includes fellow American Jess McClain and 2024 NYC winner Sheila Chepkirui. Seven-time NYC wheelchair champion Marcel Hug is also returning for another shot at the podium.Sweden's Andreas Almgren is another interesting addition, particularly because nobody has seen him race a marathon yet. The world half marathon champion has been running more than 135 miles a week to prepare for New York and told Runner's World that he's feeling confident about the work he's put in. Still, he isn't pretending the jump to 26.2 miles comes with any guarantees."The marathon is a different beast," Almgren said. "You don't really know until you're reaching that 35K mark if you're going to make it or not."And the celebrity lineup covers quite a bit of ground outside professional running. Academy Award winner Jennifer Connelly is returning to the course, along with Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski, Tony-winning Broadway star Patina Miller, and former New York Giants running back Tiki Barber.

extraction.body: The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon takes place on Sunday, November 1, bringing nearly 60,000 runners from around the world to the streets of New York for one of the most iconic races on the international running calendar. The professional women’s race is scheduled to start at 8:35 a.m. Follow this live results guide for real-time updates on the men’s and women’s winners, finishing times, podium finishers and official standings. The winners of the 2026 New York City Marathon have not yet been confirmed. The men’s and women’s results tables below will be updated in real time as the competition unfolds, with the official champions, finishing times and final standings added once they are verified. The results will be updated throughout race day as athletes cross the finish line. Final positions and finishing times will be checked against the official New York Road Runners results. Follow the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon as the elite runners compete across Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan. For live runner tracking, visit NYRR Live Results. For verified finishing times and final standings, check the official NYRR results portal. He will try to become the first men’s runner since John Kagwe in 1998 to win consecutive New York City Marathon titles. European interest centers on the Netherlands’ Abdi Nageeye (2:04:20) and Sweden’s Andreas Almgren, who is making his marathon debut after establishing himself on the track and in the half marathon. Kenya’s Hellen Obiri is the leading name in the women’s competition. She returns after winning in 2023 and 2025, when she set the course record of 2:19:51. Her main challengers include compatriots Sheila Chepkirui, the 2024 champion with a personal best of 2:17:19, and Viola Cheptoo (2:19:05). Ethiopia’s Gotytom Gebreslase (2:18:11) and American runner Jessica McClain (2:22:43) are also among the names to watch. These are pre-race contenders, not confirmed 2026 winners. The final positions and times will be published only after they are verified. The race takes place on Sunday, November 1, with professional and mass-participation divisions starting at different times. The 2026 race falls on the same day that daylight saving time ends in the United States. Clocks move back one hour at 2:00 a.m., so New York will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST) when the marathon begins. The New York Road Runners (NYRR), the race organizer, provides the official results and runner-tracking services. The men’s and women’s champions, finishing times and final podium positions will be added to this article as the official information becomes available.

It goes without saying that the annual New York City Marathon is one of the most special days of the year: uniting strangers, both spectators and runners alike, in the pursuit of 26.2 miles. Traditionally taking place on the first Sunday of November, this year’s TCS New York City Marathon lands on November 1, kicking off at 8:00 a.m. EST for the professional wheelchair and handcycle divisions, with the pros assembling at the starting line next — followed by five waves of amateur runners. If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay. – Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost. – Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed. – $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor. According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.” Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir. Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park. Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31. At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99. Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release. If you don’t plan on finding yourself in the Big Apple on November 1, there’s still a way to catch the action and camaraderie live by streaming the New York City Marathon online. It will be broadcast on WABC-TV locally and on ESPN2 nationally; cable cutters, though, can tune in with the help of a few editor-recommended streaming platforms like DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV . All of them have free trials attached for watching the marathon without having to pay.
– Starting at $59.99/month – Five-day free trial – Over 185 channels

ESPN2 is found in all of DirecTV’s main packages, from Entertainment to the well-rounded Premier that comes with over 185 channels. Thanks to the streamer’s generous, $30-off deal on new users’ first month of service, plans start at just $59.99 a month (for the aforementioned Entertainment option). That being said, DirecTV is also providing a five-day free trial . Use it to stream the 2026 New York City Marathon online at no cost.
– Starting at $63.99/month – One-day free trial – Over 200 channels

Another mode of watching the TCS New York City Marathon without cable involves signing up for Fubo’s free trial , which lasts a day. ESPN2 is included in its Pro and Elite channel bundles, which typically go for $88.99 and $98.99 per month but are also being marked down as we speak (to a first-month price of $63.99 and $68.99, respectively). The best news is that ESPN Unlimited accompanies the subscription, granting expanded access to all ESPN content: meaning you can continue enjoying your favorite spectator sports long after the marathon is completed.
– $99.99/month – Three-day free trial – Over 100 channels

Hulu + Live TV just revived its three-day free trial , so there’s no better time than now to get on board and start streaming. It carries both regular ESPN and ESPN2 for watching the NYC Marathon , not to mention over a hundred other popular channel selections like ABC, NBC, CNN, and Fox. After the trial wraps up, Hulu + Live TV will clock in at $99.99 a month. Disney+ and Hulu’s entire portfolio of TV shows plus movies will also be yours to savor.

According to New York Road Runners , this year’s professional athlete field for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon features “three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists, and 22 national record holders.”

Defending champions Hellen Obiri, Benson Kipruto, and Marcel Hug will “return to headline the women’s open division and men’s open and wheelchair divisions,” joined by notable names like Sheila Chepkirui, Sifan Hassan, Geoffrey Kamworor, Abdi Nageeye, Daniel Romanchuk, and David Weir.

Nearly 60,000 participants are set to run the course this year, chosen from a pool of over 240,000 applicants as part of New York Road Runners’ highly competitive selection process. If history is any indication, they will be cheered on by approximately two million spectators, who can always be counted on to line the streets, handmade signs in tow, and support the athletes — until the very last runner crosses the finish line in Central Park.

Each year, the NYC Marathon also attracts many an A-lister. 2026’s celebrity lineup includes Jennifer Connelly, Joshua Bassett, Antoni Porowski, Dylan Efron, Tiki Barber, Zarna Garg, Del Water Gap, and beyond. High-profile runners have also been known to register under fake names, and there’s speculation going around that Harry Styles will be among the throng, with his 30-night Madison Square Garden residency ending just a day earlier on October 31.

At the 2025 New York City Marathon, Obiri won the women’s race and set a course record while wearing the On Cloudboom Strike LS shoe. Kipruto, for this part, took home the men’s win in what was deemed the closest result for that category in marathon history: finishing 0.16 seconds faster than Alexander Mutiso Munyao. He had the Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 shoe on, which was also spotted on winners’ feet at marathons across Tokyo, London, Berlin, and Chicago last year.

New Balance continues to be the athletic footwear sponsor of both the New York Road Runners and the TCS New York City Marathon. The New Balance FuelCell SC Elite v6 model is the official race-day super shoe for New Balance athletes at the 2026 NYC Marathon, and you can buy it online on New Balance’s site for $289.99.

Other anticipated footwear sightings during the grand event (called “the best day of the year, in the best city in the world” by New York Road Runners) span the re-engineered Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 from Adidas ( dropping online on October 29 at 9:00 a.m. EST), Nike’s Alphafly 3 road-racing style, and Brooks’ carbon-plated Hyperion Elite 6 release.
Get inspired by the best of the best in running — and their sneaker choices — by watching the New York City Marathon on November 1, courtesy of DirecTV , Fubo , and Hulu + Live TV .

extraction.body: On Sunday, November 1, nearly 60,000 runners taking on the New York City Marathon will get the rare privilege of having city traffic stop for them as they cover 26.2 miles through the five boroughs. And with coverage stretching from early morning into Sunday night, you don't necessarily have to be standing along First Avenue or waiting near Central Park to catch everyone in action.Here's what you need to know about watching the race, including start times, broadcasts, and how to follow individual runners.What Time Does the 2026 NYC Marathon Start?Things get going at 8 a.m. Handcycles and select athletes with disabilities start at 8:22 a.m., before the professional women take off at 8:35 a.m. and the men follow at 9:05 a.m.The rest of the field will leave Staten Island in five waves, beginning at 9:10 a.m. and continuing through 11:30 a.m.How to Watch the 2026 NYC MarathonThe main national broadcast starts at 8 a.m. ET on ESPN2, with coverage running until 11:30 a.m. If you'd rather stream, the ESPN app has the same coverage with an ESPN Unlimited plan, plus an extra hour of prerace programming beginning at 7 a.m. and more action through 1 p.m. There's a Spanish-language feed during the main 8 to 11:30 a.m. window as well.In New York and the surrounding tri-state area, ABC7/WABC-TV is another option. Coverage begins at 7 a.m., ahead of the race broadcast from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., which you can also stream on the ABC 7 New York app.For anyone more interested in the finish line than the rest of the course, ABC7NY.com and the ABC 7 New York app have you covered from 10:30 a.m. until 6 p.m. with a dedicated live stream. That should give you plenty of time to catch the professionals and stick around for the thousands of other runners making their way into Central Park.ABC also has a national Live from the TCS New York City Marathon special scheduled for 3 to 5 p.m. Before hopping on the subway, you'll probably want to check how far along they are, which is where the official New York Road Runners app comes in handy.You can track individual runners throughout the race, check their progress at timing points, and pull up leaderboards and results. The app is available for iOS and Android, and it also has live feeds for each of the four professional races if you want to keep an eye on the elites while you're out cheering.Who to Watch at the 2026 NYC MarathonLast year's champions, Benson Kipruto and Hellen Obiri, are both coming back, and each has a memorable performance to defend. Kipruto won the closest men's finish in NYC Marathon history in 2025, while Obiri ran 2:19:51 to break the women's course record that had stood for 22 years.Conner Mantz and Zouhair Talbi are among the Americans to watch in the men's race. On the women's side, Weini Kelati is making her marathon debut against a field that includes fellow American Jess McClain and 2024 NYC winner Sheila Chepkirui. Seven-time NYC wheelchair champion Marcel Hug is also returning for another shot at the podium.Sweden's Andreas Almgren is another interesting addition, particularly because nobody has seen him race a marathon yet. The world half marathon champion has been running more than 135 miles a week to prepare for New York and told Runner's World that he's feeling confident about the work he's put in. Still, he isn't pretending the jump to 26.2 miles comes with any guarantees."The marathon is a different beast," Almgren said. "You don't really know until you're reaching that 35K mark if you're going to make it or not."And the celebrity lineup covers quite a bit of ground outside professional running. Academy Award winner Jennifer Connelly is returning to the course, along with Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski, Tony-winning Broadway star Patina Miller, and former New York Giants running back Tiki Barber.

sources.title: Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders hires an agent for first time, adding more fuel to trade rumors
passages: Shedeur Sanders has hired an NFL agent for the first time, and while that typically sounds like something a player wanting a new contract would do, that isn't the main reason the Cleveland Browns quarterback is making this move.

BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QUARTERBACK DESPITE HOME CROWD BOOING AND HIS '17 AWAY GAMES' COMMENTS But the fact that Sanders is hiring an agent now, after going through the draft process, enduring a disappointing first day in which he hoped to be selected in the first round but fell to the fifth and signing his rookie deal without representation, is curious.
Watson, 31, hasn't been great in leading the Browns to a 3-2 record.
The point is the picture of the Browns' offense is not one that suggests Watson is on the verge of getting benched and Sanders promoted.
Sanders, in only his second season since being drafted in 2025, has hired Adie von Gontard of Young Money APAA Sports, as his first NFL representation.
The new agent would then deal with the team on the player's behalf in requesting a trade — which is rarely a pleasant conversation.
It should be noted the NFL is rife with rumors and none of the sources speaking about Sanders are directly tied to his family.
Sanders currently finds himself as the backup quarterback in Cleveland after losing a competition for the starting job to veteran Deshaun Watson.
Sanders has mostly stepped back into the shadows as most backup quarterbacks do.

extraction.body: Shedeur Sanders has hired an NFL agent for the first time, and while that typically sounds like something a player wanting a new contract would do, that isn't the main reason the Cleveland Browns quarterback is making this move. Sanders, in only his second season since being drafted in 2025, has hired Adie von Gontard of Young Money APAA Sports, as his first NFL representation. This is a logical choice because Gontard already represents Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter. Hunter and Sanders were teammates and friends at the University of Colorado and came out in the same 2025 draft. BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QUARTERBACK DESPITE HOME CROWD BOOING AND HIS '17 AWAY GAMES' COMMENTS But the fact that Sanders is hiring an agent now, after going through the draft process, enduring a disappointing first day in which he hoped to be selected in the first round but fell to the fifth and signing his rookie deal without representation, is curious. But multiple NFL sources are telling OutKick they believe Sanders has hired representation because he's getting ready to press for a trade from the Cleveland Browns. It should be noted the NFL is rife with rumors and none of the sources speaking about Sanders are directly tied to his family. DESHAUN WATSON REMAINS THE CLEVELAND BROWNS STARTING QUARTERBACK BUT THAT COMES WITH AN EXPIRATION DATE Only two weeks ago, Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hired an agent for the first time and over the weekend the Houston Texans confirmed they had traded for him. Minkah Fitzpatrick (2019), Za'Darius Smith (2023) and Haason Reddick (2024) all hired new agents because they were trying to get traded. Sanders currently finds himself as the backup quarterback in Cleveland after losing a competition for the starting job to veteran Deshaun Watson. Coach Todd Monken's decision to start Watson was not unexpected, but nonetheless disappointing to Sanders. Sanders has mostly stepped back into the shadows as most backup quarterbacks do. That opportunity, however, doesn’t appear to be on the horizon in Cleveland. Watson, 31, hasn't been great in leading the Browns to a 3-2 record. And, yes, Cleveland's 93 total points is bottom 10 in the league. But some of that is surely on the fact the Browns offensive line has been inconsistent, coach Todd Monken's offense is a work in progress and the running game is middling. The point is the picture of the Browns' offense is not one that suggests Watson is on the verge of getting benched and Sanders promoted. Or he can grit his teeth, stay quiet and hire an agent to do something on his behalf. The new agent would then deal with the team on the player's behalf in requesting a trade — which is rarely a pleasant conversation. It makes sense if Sanders wants an opportunity elsewhere, he hire someone to make that case on his behalf instead of fighting the battle himself. So, yes, the timing of the agent hiring raises eyebrows. It adds smoke to rumors that were already smoldering.

extraction.body: While Shedeur Sanders made a move this week that seemingly signals a trade from the Cleveland Browns could be coming, a top NFL insider has shut down the possibility before next month's NFL trade deadline. To the joy of Browns fans, the team enters their game on the Week 6 NFL schedule against rivals the Baltimore Ravens with a 3-2 record. For a fanbase used to losing, being over .500 at this point in the season and actually having hope to compete for a playoff spot is reason for celebration. Yet, one player who may not be thrilled is Sanders. The youngster lost the QB battle this summer to Deshaun Watson, despite the objections of fans. And so far, the veteran QB has played well enough that he is not in danger of being benched. It means that, barring injury, Sanders won't play in games again until next year. That may be why he decided to hire an agent for the first time in his career this week. The move immediately created speculation that the quarterback turned to a professional negotiator to set up his exit from Cleveland so he can get an opportunity elsewhere before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. However, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported on Saturday, "After talking to multiple league and team sources, I'd be surprised if he dealt quarterback Shedeur Sanders before this year's trade deadline." Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images On paper, it makes sense to trade Sanders. If he couldn't beat out Watson, coming off two Achilles surgeries, for the starting job this summer, he probably doesn't have a serious future in Cleveland. Furthermore, if they got a strong offer from a QB-needy team, then they should make that trade. However, it is hard to trust that Watson will remain healthy for the rest of the season when he has never done that during his five years with the Browns. Sooner or later he will probably miss games this season, and having a backup they can trust to hopefully keep them in the playoff hunt has value. If the Browns began to slip from the playoff picture before the deadline, maybe moving Sanders makes more sense. However, a case could also be made that it is a reason not to trade him, because he could just be promoted to the starting job to try and salvage their postseason hopes in the second half of the season.

passages: Cleveland Browns Trade Pitch Deals Shedeur Sanders With the Browns having Deshaun Watson firmly as their starting quarterback, they could look to trade Sanders, and the Philadelphia Eagles could be a landing spot.
Shedeur Sanders' name has come up in trade rumors, especially after he hired an agent.
The Cleveland Browns could trade away one of their four quarterbacks.
Analyst Explains Sanders Mock Trade The proposed deal from Rotman makes sense, and he believes Cleveland is open to moving on from Sanders, who seemingly also wants out.
Philadelphia, meanwhile, acquires Sanders to either back up Tanner McKee or take over as the starter amid Hurts' absence.

Getting a draft pick in exchange for a player who probably wants to be elsewhere and who the Browns don't seem eager to put onto the field in a meaningful capacity sounds like a no-brainer to me." It isn't a major trade, but the Browns are fine having a quarterback room of Watson, Gabriel, and Green going forward, which makes Sanders expendable.
As he gets closer to a return, the Browns will have to make a roster decision, and it could involve a trade.
"Sanders likely wants out, and why shouldn't the Browns grant him his wish if they're actually comfortable with Watson?
Cleveland made a surprise move, carrying all four quarterbacks, but Dillon Gabriel began the year on the injured reserve.

The cost is also fair, as Cleveland selected him in the fifth round, so they get the same draft pick back. Analyst Explains Sanders Mock Trade The proposed deal from Rotman makes sense, and he believes Cleveland is open to moving on from Sanders, who seemingly also wants out. "Sanders likely wants out, and why shouldn't the Browns grant him his wish if they're actually comfortable with Watson? They'd still have Dillon Gabriel internally, giving them a young quarterback to turn to if Watson falters or goes down with an injury, and can net a draft pick in exchange for a player who, if we're being honest, the Browns likely don't want to see a single meaningful snap this season at all," Rotman wrote. "A fifth-round pick might seem insignificant on the surface, but the Browns used a fifth-rounder on Sanders himself in 2025. Sanders likely wants out, and the Browns don't seem interested in playing him. Getting a draft pick in exchange for a player who probably wants to be elsewhere and who the Browns don't seem eager to put onto the field in a meaningful capacity sounds like a no-brainer to me." It isn't a major trade, but the Browns are fine having a quarterback room of Watson, Gabriel, and Green going forward, which makes Sanders expendable.

Minkah Fitzpatrick (2019), Za'Darius Smith (2023) and Haason Reddick (2024) all hired new agents because they were trying to get traded. Sanders currently finds himself as the backup quarterback in Cleveland after losing a competition for the starting job to veteran Deshaun Watson. Coach Todd Monken's decision to start Watson was not unexpected, but nonetheless disappointing to Sanders. Sanders has mostly stepped back into the shadows as most backup quarterbacks do. And, yes, Cleveland's 93 total points is bottom 10 in the league. But some of that is surely on the fact the Browns offensive line has been inconsistent, coach Todd Monken's offense is a work in progress and the running game is middling. The point is the picture of the Browns' offense is not one that suggests Watson is on the verge of getting benched and Sanders promoted. Or he can grit his teeth, stay quiet and hire an agent to do something on his behalf. The new agent would then deal with the team on the player's behalf in requesting a trade — which is rarely a pleasant conversation. It makes sense if Sanders wants an opportunity elsewhere, he hire someone to make that case on his behalf instead of fighting the battle himself. So, yes, the timing of the agent hiring raises eyebrows. It adds smoke to rumors that were already smoldering.

extraction.body: While Shedeur Sanders made a move this week that seemingly signals a trade from the Cleveland Browns could be coming, a top NFL insider has shut down the possibility before next month's NFL trade deadline. To the joy of Browns fans, the team enters their game on the Week 6 NFL schedule against rivals the Baltimore Ravens with a 3-2 record. For a fanbase used to losing, being over .500 at this point in the season and actually having hope to compete for a playoff spot is reason for celebration. Yet, one player who may not be thrilled is Sanders. The youngster lost the QB battle this summer to Deshaun Watson, despite the objections of fans. And so far, the veteran QB has played well enough that he is not in danger of being benched. It means that, barring injury, Sanders won't play in games again until next year. That may be why he decided to hire an agent for the first time in his career this week. The move immediately created speculation that the quarterback turned to a professional negotiator to set up his exit from Cleveland so he can get an opportunity elsewhere before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. However, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported on Saturday, "After talking to multiple league and team sources, I'd be surprised if he dealt quarterback Shedeur Sanders before this year's trade deadline." Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images On paper, it makes sense to trade Sanders. If he couldn't beat out Watson, coming off two Achilles surgeries, for the starting job this summer, he probably doesn't have a serious future in Cleveland. Furthermore, if they got a strong offer from a QB-needy team, then they should make that trade. However, it is hard to trust that Watson will remain healthy for the rest of the season when he has never done that during his five years with the Browns. Sooner or later he will probably miss games this season, and having a backup they can trust to hopefully keep them in the playoff hunt has value. If the Browns began to slip from the playoff picture before the deadline, maybe moving Sanders makes more sense. However, a case could also be made that it is a reason not to trade him, because he could just be promoted to the starting job to try and salvage their postseason hopes in the second half of the season.
